a0.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) (press statement)
a0.name: World Health Organization (WHO) (press statement)
a0.speech: Appealed to the United States government to exempt HIV treatment from its current funding pause ; expressed concern over the immediate suspension of funding for HIV programmes in low- and middle-income countries ; "A funding halt for HIV programmes can put people living with HIV at immediate increased risk of illness and death and undermine efforts to prevent transmission in communities and countries" ; explained that a long-term funding pause could have devastating consequences, including a surge in new HIV infections and deaths, and could reverse decades of progress, potentially taking the world back to the 1980s and 1990s when millions died of HIV every year globally, including many in the United States ; further stated that the global community would also suffer significant setbacks in its efforts to combat HIV, undermining partnerships and investments in cutting-edge research, diagnostics, and treatment ; noted that the sudden and prolonged stop to PEPFAR programmes could lead to a surge in new infections and deaths, reversing decades of progress in the fight against HIV ; expressed deep concern about the implications of the funding pause, emphasising the need for a managed transition to minimise the impact on people living with HIV, and reinstated its commitment to supporting PEPFAR and other partners in managing change processes effectively

a57.speaker: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera, President of Malawi
a57.name: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera
a57.title: President of Malawi
a57.speech: In a statement accompanying the announcement of the cabinet reshuffle, emphasized the importance of accountability and performance in public office, and reiterated his commitment to addressing the gaps exposed by the Chilima Inquiry to restore public confidence in his administration's ability to manage crises effectively.

a57.speaker: Dr. Henry Chibambo, Political Analyst
a57.name: Dr. Henry Chibambo
a57.title: Political Analyst
a57.speech: "The cabinet reshuffle is a positive step, but the success of these changes will depend on how effectively the new appointees address the challenges in their respective ministries."

a67.speaker: US State Department (press statement)
a67.name: US State Department (press statement)
a67.speech: Said that the top US diplomat, Marco Rubio, "emphasized the importance of relations between the United States and Benin and welcomed Benin's cooperation on regional security." Said the two men also "discussed shared priorities," including strengthening democratic governance and promoting stability in West Africa.

a149.speaker: Awach sub-county residents
a149.name: Awach sub-county residents
a149.speech: Say that following the rehabilitation of the road, they can now have access to basic services like markets, schools, and health facilities.

a149.speaker: Charles Omugetum, Acting Deputy Chief Administrative Officer, Abim District
a149.name: Charles Omugetum
a149.title: Acting Deputy Chief Administrative Officer, Abim District
a149.speech: Says that several people lost their lives in the hands of cattle rustlers who were using the road to carry out attacks.

a149.speaker: Charles Omugetum, Acting Deputy Chief Administrative Officer, Abim District
a149.name: Charles Omugetum
a149.title: Acting Deputy Chief Administrative Officer, Abim District
a149.speech: Warned the residents against using ox-ploughs on the road while going to the garden: “Some of these local are stubborn because as they are going to the garden they plough the road. You should plough the garden not the road so that it can stay for three, four, or five years because as a district we have very meager resources, the money that we were supposed to bring here should be taken somewhere else to work on other areas such that children and mothers in that area can access markets, schools and health facilities easily.”

a149.speaker: Charles Arube, District Engineer
a149.name: Charles Arube
a149.title: District Engineer
a149.speech: Said that the district will avail insufficient resources for routine maintenance of the road.

a149.speaker: Olive D’Mello, Acting Head of Programming at Catholic Relief Services (CRS)
a149.name: Olive D’Mello
a149.title: Acting Head of Programming at Catholic Relief Services (CRS)
a149.speech: Noted that the communities in Karamoja face different shocks and stresses, including drought, flooding, water scarcity, conflicts with the associated insecurity, which she says is “compounded by the impact of poor road infrastructure makes it difficult for the communities to access basic services like markets, schools, and health facilities.”

a149.speaker: Olive D’Mello, Acting Head of Programming at Catholic Relief Services (CRS)
a149.name: Olive D’Mello
a149.title: Acting Head of Programming at Catholic Relief Services (CRS)
a149.speech: “Catholic Relief Services is proud to have been associated with this joint venture and are pleased that the local government has included this access road in their inventory of public works and is making the necessary budgetary provision to sustain its maintenance over time” ; said all the road works that CRS has worked on in Karamoja are part of the greater achievements of the $43.6 million USAID funded Nuyok program.

a149.speaker: Chip Bury, Senior Humanitarian Assistance Officer at USAID
a149.name: Chip Bury
a149.title: Senior Humanitarian Assistance Officer at USAID
a149.speech: Says they invested in the road to boost household incomes because “the USAID Nuyok project has worked on many issues in the region and it has addressed the nutrition needs of pregnant and lactating women and children under the age of two, boosting household incomes and mobilizing communities to advocate for improved governance on issues related to food and nutrition in the region.”

a258.speaker: "Long-Term Studies - The Development Strategy" (document published by the SECP in November 1979)
a258.name: "Long-Term Studies - The Development Strategy" (document published by the SECP in November 1979)
a258.speech: Began with a strategic diagnosis of the country's situation: at the economic level there was a great imbalance between national production and consumption and capital formation (assessed at 40% in 1977), covered by emigrants' remittances and Official Development Assistance; at the social level, the emigration of the most dynamic and qualified elements of the population favoured the maintenance of the social hierarchy inherited from the colonial past ; set out the vision of "the construction, by the end of the century (2000), of an economy capable of offering every Cape Verdean the possibility of living in the Archipelago with a standard of living sufficient not to be obliged to emigrate because of unemployment and misery."

a258.speaker: "Revision of long-term development prospects" (study published by the SECP, August 1984)
a258.name: "Revision of long-term development prospects" (study published by the SECP
a258.title: August 1984)
a258.speech: Showed the need to adjust some objectives of the first long-term study, such as reducing irrigated areas in 2000 from 10,000 to 4,000 hectares and abandoning the objective of full employment by the end of the century ; showed that Cape Verde would face in the long term a number of challenges which, if unresolved, could endanger its sustainability as an independent state, and that it had to create a strong and diversified productive apparatus to reduce its dependence on rainfall and on foreign aid.

a258.speaker: National Council of the PAICV
a258.name: National Council of the PAICV
a258.speech: Recommended, in June 1985, a "broad national discussion" of the conclusions of the study on long-term prospects.

a258.speaker: Jose Brito, former Deputy Minister of Cooperation and Planning (author)
a258.name: Jose Brito
a258.title: former Deputy Minister of Cooperation and Planning (author)
a258.speech: As I stated in the presentation of the first NDP: "There must be the broadest possible concertation between the planning services and all of their partners. The effectiveness of the whole planning process depends on the richness and permanence of this concertation."

a404.speaker: Molete Selete, former Maseru City Council (MCC) Town Clerk
a404.name: Molete Selete
a404.title: former Maseru City Council (MCC) Town Clerk
a404.speech: Has accused Principal Secretary of Local Government, Chieftainship, Home Affairs and Police, Mamphaka Mabesa, of having orchestrated his arrest over the “trumped up charges” that he says were bound to fail; claimed he believed Dr Mabesa had collaborated with the Directorate on Corruption and Economic Offences (DCEO) to have him arrested. He claims that prior to his arrest last year, he had been instructed by the PS to go and work at the Lesotho Mounted Police Service (LMPS), a directive he refused, insisting that he was employed by MCC, not the police ; “There was an effort to remove me from MCC and have me stationed at the police. But I refused because I'm employed at MCC” ; “The DCEO interrogated everyone at MCC, then finally arrested me and took me to court the next day. After being granted bail, I received a show cause letter on 30 April, and the next day I was suspended. The PS personally delivered the letter.” ; “What's surprising is that I was the only one suspended, yet I was charged along with other MCC employees—one being a consultant and the other a City Engineer. I don't know the motive behind my arrest. I can't say it was solely the DCEO or the PS, but the connections are there.”

a404.speaker: Molete Selete, former Maseru City Council (MCC) Town Clerk
a404.name: Molete Selete
a404.title: former Maseru City Council (MCC) Town Clerk
a404.speech: Also criticised the DCEO for failing to inform the public when the charges were dropped: “They accused me of fraud, corruption, and money laundering—serious charges. But when the case was withdrawn, the DCEO didn't call the media like they did when they arrested us. Our names remain tainted as if we stole government funds” ; “We paid people who were supposed to be paid. There was no evidence that we personally benefited from the money. So why were we taken to court? Was someone pushing a personal vendetta?” ; said the DCEO cited lack of sufficient evidence as the reason for withdrawing the case ; “Where did they get the intelligence to begin with? Was it from the same person who wanted me reassigned to the police? You don't take a case to court without solid evidence.”

a404.speaker: DCEO charge sheet (court record)
a404.name: DCEO charge sheet (court record)
a404.speech: According to the charge sheet, Mr Selete, Mr Tikoe, and MCC consultant Molefe Nthabane “illegally authorised” an advance payment of M14 million to the SCIGM-SMGC Joint Venture and Mr Leong despite knowing that the company had not submitted the mandatory 20 percent advance payment guarantee on the total contract value of about M75 million.

a404.speaker: Directorate on Corruption and Economic Offences (DCEO)
a404.name: Directorate on Corruption and Economic Offences (DCEO)
a404.speech: Maintained that the payment was illegal and fraudulent due to the absence of an authentic advance payment guarantee; has refuted Mr Selete's allegations, promising to re-enroll the charges once it completes its probe.

a404.speaker: Mamphaka Mabesa, Principal Secretary of Local Government, Chieftainship, Home Affairs and Police
a404.name: Mamphaka Mabesa
a404.title: Principal Secretary of Local Government, Chieftainship, Home Affairs and Police
a404.speech: When contacted for comment, simply declined saying, “No comment”.

a404.speaker: 'Matlhokomelo Senoko, DCEO spokesperson
a404.name: 'Matlhokomelo Senoko
a404.title: DCEO spokesperson
a404.speech: Denied the allegations, insisting that the DCEO had relaunched investigations and would return the matter to court. “The case has been withdrawn, not dissolved. At any time when DCEO is ready, they can be charged again” ; “The fact that the case has been withdrawn does not mean there is no evidence. We have a serious corruption case to pursue. Once sufficient evidence is secured, they will be prosecuted” ; she dismissed allegations that the DCEO colluded with the PS as “not true”.

a417.speaker: Epiphane Gildéric Adjovi, economist
a417.name: Epiphane Gildéric Adjovi
a417.title: economist
a417.speech: Said the resurgence of protectionism observed on the part of the United States since President Donald Trump's return to power constitutes a major economic event that deserves in-depth analysis, and that the decision can be considered a calling into question of the tariff preference granted by the United States to certain countries, including Benin, through AGOA. "Although the share of the United States in our exports is still fairly small (a little less than 2% between 2021 and 2023), it is showing a very marked upward trend." ; "The abandonment of AGOA and the establishment of a 10% customs duty will inevitably lead to increased competition for the products we export to that country. This may contribute to a reduction in our exports to the United States. The consequence must be a worsening of the deficit in Benin's trade balance, which is structurally in deficit."

a417.speaker: Epiphane Gildéric Adjovi, economist
a417.name: Epiphane Gildéric Adjovi
a417.title: economist
a417.speech: Said that despite the relative weakness of the share of Beninese sales on the American market, the measure could have notable repercussions on several macroeconomic indicators: "One can notably expect a contraction of investment in sectors oriented towards export to the United States, a fall in the incomes of the producers concerned, as well as a decrease in the volume of goods transiting through Benin bound for the American market. This last development could also negatively impact the country's port activities."

a417.speaker: Epiphane Gildéric Adjovi, economist
a417.name: Epiphane Gildéric Adjovi
a417.title: economist
a417.speech: Said on the Glo-Djigbé Industrial Zone (Gdiz) textile sector that "it is too early to have a fairly precise estimate of the impact on the activities of the textile factories installed at the Gdiz," but that since conquering the American market is among investors' objectives there, "there is a risk of a slowdown in foreign investment," while adequate trade facilitation measures could improve competitiveness and attract investors ; "From my point of view, the situation should not be dramatised... our capacity to react can prevent our economy from suffering a significant slowdown in its growth rate."

a417.speaker: Epiphane Gildéric Adjovi, economist
a417.name: Epiphane Gildéric Adjovi
a417.title: economist
a417.speech: Argued that the response "must not be limited to seeking a short-term readjustment," because obtaining new unilateral preferences through bilateral renegotiation "will always expose Benin to the possibility of an abrupt reversal in the future"; urged continuation of the policy of diversifying export products and markets and the elimination of all practices and measures that obstruct competitiveness, so as to make the country "more resilient in the face of trade policy shocks from its partners."

a417.speaker: Epiphane Gildéric Adjovi, economist
a417.name: Epiphane Gildéric Adjovi
a417.title: economist
a417.speech: Said on the fate of AGOA that the United States has, since President Trump's return, taken measures suggesting it is "no longer in a logic of special and differential treatment for developing countries — I am speaking of the suspension of the programmes managed by USAID," and that clarifications must be given by the American side ; proposed that the authorities assume AGOA will not be renewed after September 2025 and begin taking measures so as not to be excluded from the American market through lack of competitiveness.

a417.speaker: Epiphane Gildéric Adjovi, economist
a417.name: Epiphane Gildéric Adjovi
a417.title: economist
a417.speech: Said such shocks create the conditions for a readjustment of economic strategies and that countries must avoid building their entire strategy on preferential agreements, since "unilateral preferences can be called into question at any time"; pointed to the AfCFTA as a mechanism for better access to the African market, and noted that Benin's membership of WAEMU, ECOWAS and the AU requires a concerted trade policy approach, since "the regional approach also increases our negotiating power."

a656.speaker: Mwandida Theu, Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.name: Mwandida Theu
a656.title: Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.speech: "I am Youth and Society [YAS] programme coordinator for human rights and civil society strengthening. I lead programmes that cultivate a new generation of human rights defenders, mobilise youth participation in governance, anti-corruption, rule of law and advocate for the rights of marginalised groups, including refugees and migrants."

a656.speaker: Mwandida Theu, Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.name: Mwandida Theu
a656.title: Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.speech: Reflected on her appointment as Commissioner: "It symbolised recognition for the work I have been doing in human rights advocacy, youth activism and it reinforced my belief in the power of young people to shape the future of our country."

a656.speaker: Mwandida Theu, Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.name: Mwandida Theu
a656.title: Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.speech: Shared some of the challenges she has faced as a young commissioner, particularly navigating the generational gap within decision-making spaces: "Often, the perspectives and experiences of young people are undervalued and it can be difficult to have our voices acknowledged by those who have been in leadership positions for years." ; "To overcome this, I have learned to assert myself confidently and use evidence-based arguments to advocate for youth-inclusive solutions. I have also built trust and credibility with other commissioners and stakeholders which helped bridge the gap as they come to realise that young people can contribute valuable insights and fresh perspectives to these critical issues."

a656.speaker: Mwandida Theu, Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.name: Mwandida Theu
a656.title: Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.speech: Highlighted that her role as a human rights advocate has been fuelled by a commitment to justice and equity: "A few key experiences stand out as catalysts for my passion. One of the most significant was during the development of Malawi's first-ever National Youth Manifesto in 2018. As the coordinator for the youth decide campaign, I led efforts to gather views and demands of young people, translating them into a unified manifesto." ; added that the process was eye-opening as it allowed her to travel to various districts, engage with youth from diverse backgrounds, and hear their frustrations and aspirations firsthand.

a656.speaker: Mwandida Theu, Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.name: Mwandida Theu
a656.title: Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.speech: "I prioritice creating safe and inclusive spaces where everyone feels valued and heard using gender-responsive facilitation techniques, encouraging open dialogue and inviting women and youths to take part in discussions."

a656.speaker: Mwandida Theu, Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.name: Mwandida Theu
a656.title: Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.speech: "Over the next few years, I hope to see an increase in the participation of youth and women in politics not just as voters, but as active decision-makers and candidates for public office." ; "I envision the dismantling of systemic barriers that prevent women and young people from entering the political arena such as gender-based violence, cultural norms that discourage women's leadership, and the lack of access to resources for youth to engage in political campaigns." ; hopes to see the implementation of more robust policies that encourage youth and women to take leadership roles such as affirmative action policies and gender quotas within political parties and government institutions, and more platforms that empower young people and women to be politically active and informed.

a656.speaker: Mwandida Theu, Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.name: Mwandida Theu
a656.title: Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.speech: Added that electoral reforms are essential for making the political process more accessible to marginalised groups, including lowering the cost of running for office, increasing transparency in campaign financing and providing support for young and first-time candidates who may not have financial backing.

a656.speaker: Mwandida Theu, Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.name: Mwandida Theu
a656.title: Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.speech: Said balancing her roles as a youth activist, commissioner and advocate requires time management and focus.

a656.speaker: Mwandida Theu, Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.name: Mwandida Theu
a656.title: Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.speech: Advised young women aspiring to engage in activism and leadership to be fearless and persistent in pursuing their passion: "The road may be challenging, especially in a world that often discourages women from taking on leadership roles, but it's crucial to stay focused and resilient. Educate yourself, build your skills, and always seek opportunities to grow." ; "Every voice counts and sometimes, it only takes one person to ignite change. Activism and leadership are not just about being on the front lines, but also about building partnerships and collaborating with others."

a656.speaker: Mwandida Theu, Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.name: Mwandida Theu
a656.title: Malawi Peace and Unity commissioner, youth activist and human rights advocate
a656.speech: Emphasized that mentorship and support networks have been essential to her journey, providing her with guidance, encouragement, and access to opportunities she may not have found on her own.

a715.speaker: Triza Nyirenda, Communication Coordinator, Youth Response for Social Change
a715.name: Triza Nyirenda
a715.title: Communication Coordinator, Youth Response for Social Change
a715.speech: Said the organisation nullifies child marriages through a project called “Social Transformation for Ending Child Marriages,” implemented in six traditional authorities in Machinga with funding from USAID ; added that Youth Response nullifies child marriages in traditional authorities, among them Nyambi, Mizinga, Chikweo, Mchinguza and Paramount Chief Kawinga ; said out of the 320 girls, 65 of them were referred to learn vocational skills to sustain their livelihood, while the rest went back to school ; “From 2021 to this year, Youth Response for Social Change nullified 320 marriages in Machinga. This is an alarming figure.”

a715.speaker: Triza Nyirenda, Communication Coordinator, Youth Response for Social Change
a715.name: Triza Nyirenda
a715.title: Communication Coordinator, Youth Response for Social Change
a715.speech: Called on the government and other organisations to collaborate in ending child marriages so that girls can go back to school to continue with their education, and said there was a need to continue supporting the girls with educational materials once they return to school to ensure they concentrate on their education.

a715.speaker: Masautso Katemera, Inspector and Community Policing Coordinator, Machinga Police Station
a715.name: Masautso Katemera
a715.title: Inspector and Community Policing Coordinator, Machinga Police Station
a715.speech: Said child marriage is a concern in Machinga due to poverty and cultural practices ; said police continue to engage communities on the negative implications of child marriages, and commended Youth Response NGO for taking the lead in nullifying child marriages in Machinga.

a924.speaker: Dr Amal Al-Rashed, Associate Professor in the Linguistics Section of the Department of Arabic Language and Literature, King Saud University
a924.name: Dr Amal Al-Rashed
a924.title: Associate Professor in the Linguistics Section of the Department of Arabic Language and Literature, King Saud University
a924.speech: Discussed how to correctly write the open ta, the closed ta and the ha at the end of words, following an evaluation of assignments previously submitted by the trainees, a presentation and a practical application ; also spoke about writing words ending with a silent damma and words ending with tanween, with a detailed explanation of each word through presentation and practical application ; also discussed methods for correctly writing sentences and paragraphs, the characteristics of appropriate administrative sentences, good word choice, grammatical integrity, clarity and simplicity, as well as methods of writing paragraphs using linking tools and orthographically connected words.

a973.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) (press statement)
a973.name: World Food Programme (WFP) (press statement)
a973.speech: “The organisation is currently facing an alarming 40% drop in funding for 2025 compared with last year. The severity of these cuts, combined with record numbers of people in need, is leading to an unprecedented crisis for tens of millions of people around the world.”

a973.speaker: Rania Dagash-Kamara, WFP head of partnerships and innovation
a973.name: Rania Dagash-Kamara
a973.title: WFP head of partnerships and innovation
a973.speech: “WFP prioritises the countries with the greatest needs. Although we are doing everything we can to reduce operating costs, we cannot ignore it: we are facing a financial abyss with potentially fatal consequences.”

a973.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) estimates
a973.name: World Food Programme (WFP) estimates
a973.speech: According to WFP estimates, “58 million people risk losing vital assistance in the agency’s 28 most critical operations because of insufficient funding.”

a973.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a973.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a973.speech: Had already warned on Thursday that it had only two weeks of food aid left in Gaza and that famine was again threatening the region, after the resumption of Israeli military operations in Palestinian territory.

a1043.speaker: Trump Administration
a1043.name: Trump Administration
a1043.speech: has proposed cutting all funding for the African Development Bank and the African Development Fund starting in 2026.

a1043.speaker: International Trade Centre
a1043.name: International Trade Centre
a1043.speech: has described the United States' tariffs as catastrophic for developing countries.

a1043.speaker: African Development Bank (working paper released in March 2025)
a1043.name: African Development Bank (working paper released in March 2025)
a1043.speech: argued that remittances — private transfers made by migrants to relatives in their home countries — could potentially solve the financing problem.

a1043.speaker: Modelling study published in The Lancet
a1043.name: Modelling study published in The Lancet
a1043.speech: estimates that the international HIV funding crisis could lead to millions of new HIV infections and HIV-related deaths, with Mozambique, South Africa, and Uganda being significantly affected.

a1043.speaker: International Debt Report 2024
a1043.name: International Debt Report 2024
a1043.speech: reported that low- and middle-income countries face a much higher debt burden than in the previous decade, with debt servicing and interest payments consuming a significant portion of national budgets and hindering governments' ability to invest in agriculture, health, education, and the environment.

a1043.speaker: Indermit Gill, Senior Vice President and Chief Economist of the World Bank (foreword to the International Debt Report 2024, December 2024)
a1043.name: Indermit Gill
a1043.title: Senior Vice President and Chief Economist of the World Bank (foreword to the International Debt Report 2024, December 2024)
a1043.speech: “It's time to face the reality: the poorest countries facing debt distress need debt relief if they are to have a shot at lasting prosperity,” pointing out that since 2022, foreign private creditors have extracted nearly $141-billion more from public sector borrowers in developing economies in debt service payments than they have provided in new financing.

a1043.speaker: African Union
a1043.name: African Union
a1043.speech: designated this year as the Year of Reparations for Africans.

a1043.speaker: Volker Türk, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a1043.name: Volker Türk
a1043.title: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a1043.speech: has called for the June/July 2025 Fourth UN Financing for Development (FfD4) conference to acknowledge how the current debt architecture leads to human rights violations and requires urgent reform.

a1043.speaker: Anneke Meerkotter, Executive Director, Southern Africa Litigation Centre (opinion piece)
a1043.name: Anneke Meerkotter
a1043.title: Executive Director, Southern Africa Litigation Centre (opinion piece)
a1043.speech: argues that foundations alone cannot sufficiently close the financial gap left by aid cuts, that acceptance of the current situation cannot be the answer, and that African countries should refrain from paying their debts and challenge the financial systems that have led to Africa's dependency on foreign aid; “But this is not the point at which we go cap in hand to the US administration asking for a ‘deal’. We need to remain firm and united in our demands.”

a1106.speaker: Femi Babafemi, NDLEA Director of Media & Advocacy
a1106.name: Femi Babafemi
a1106.title: NDLEA Director of Media & Advocacy
a1106.speech: Disclosed in a statement on Sunday that during a joint examination of her three bags, Adrienne, who was coming to Nigeria for the first time, was found with 74 parcels of the illicit substance weighing 35.20 kilograms stuffed in two of her three bags.

a1106.speaker: National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) statement
a1106.name: National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) statement
a1106.speech: "In the same vein, NDLEA operatives at the Port Harcourt Ports, Onne, Rivers state have intercepted Thirteen Million Two Hundred and Ninety Eight Thousand (13,298,000) pills of opioids including Tramadol, Tramaking Quick Action Tramadol, Tamol-X, Royal Tapentadol and Carisoprodol as well as three hundred and thirty-eight thousand two hundred and fifty three (338, 253) bottles of codeine based cough syrup, all worth over nine billion seventeen million seven hundred and seventy one thousand naira (N9,017, 771,000) in street value. The opioids were recovered in three containers coming from India, targeted by the NDLEA during a 100% joint examination of the cargoes with men of the Nigerian Customs and other port stakeholders on Wednesday, 2nd and Thursday, 3rd October 2024."

a1106.speaker: Adrienne Munju, 41-year-old Canadian suspect (statement to NDLEA)
a1106.name: Adrienne Munju
a1106.title: 41-year-old Canadian suspect (statement to NDLEA)
a1106.speech: "In her statement, she claimed she was recruited to traffic the consignment through an online platform for 10,000 Canadian dollars upon successful delivery in Lagos. She said she took the offer because she needed the money to pay for her ongoing master's degree programme in Canada."

a1284.speaker: Modibo Kane Togo, Prefect of Niafunké
a1284.name: Modibo Kane Togo
a1284.title: Prefect of Niafunké
a1284.speech: During the introductory meetings, the prefect insisted on communication — real communication — between colleagues and, above all, on transparency in the management of State affairs.

a1284.speaker: Modibo Kane Togo, Prefect of Niafunké
a1284.name: Modibo Kane Togo
a1284.title: Prefect of Niafunké
a1284.speech: Ordered that all constructions encroaching on the streets of Niafunké be listed, demolished and rectified "without qualms"; ordered the outright demolition of illegal market installations after traders failed to respect a two-month deadline they had set themselves; declared that letting toilet waste water flow directly into the streets, sometimes past mosques, is strictly forbidden and that offenders will answer before the law; announced that all blocked ditches will be cleared and cleaned within a week and that those using gutters to dump waste have been summoned by the sanitation service and will be handled by the police after a one-month grace period.

a1284.speaker: Modibo Kane Togo, Prefect of Niafunké
a1284.name: Modibo Kane Togo
a1284.title: Prefect of Niafunké
a1284.speech: "The situation is serious, since as of today, the town of Niafunké no longer has any unsold land. This is unacceptable. Future generations have done nothing to deserve this fate."

a1284.speaker: Imam of the grand mosque of Niafunké
a1284.name: Imam of the grand mosque of Niafunké
a1284.speech: said, at the information meeting initiated by the prefect on Monday 10 March 2025: "We congratulate, support and encourage the prefect because everything he is doing benefits Niafunké."

a1284.speaker: Another customary chief of Niafunké
a1284.name: Another customary chief of Niafunké
a1284.speech: stated that one must have the honesty to tell the truth in the face of history, because everyone is complicit in this situation. "In any case, there will be malcontents (those at fault), and also happy people, those who were wronged, without any defence," he said.

a1284.speaker: Some native elders of Niafunké
a1284.name: Some native elders of Niafunké
a1284.speech: say that the town's recent administrations are a disgrace.

a1284.speaker: Residents of Niafunké
a1284.name: Residents of Niafunké
a1284.speech: Frustrated for more than a decade, they show their support for the prefect at each of his visits; women, old people and young people punctuate his passage with chants of "Anga Ta", "Ambi Ko", "Tignè debi laban", "Prefect, free Niafunké for us"; after the meeting on rectifying the town's urban development plan, the inhabitants of Niafunké expressed their hope in prefect Togo's actions.

a1355.speaker: Moussa Aden Miganeh, Prefect of the Ali-Sabieh region (representative of the public authorities in the region)
a1355.name: Moussa Aden Miganeh
a1355.title: Prefect of the Ali-Sabieh region (representative of the public authorities in the region)
a1355.speech: Underlined the importance of this workshop focused on the learning of reading in basic school. He made it known that the strengthening of reading must not stop at school and that support for it must continue into the family home with the guidance of parents.

a1355.speaker: Charmake Hassan Allaleh, President of the Ali-Sabieh regional council
a1355.name: Charmake Hassan Allaleh
a1355.title: President of the Ali-Sabieh regional council
a1355.speech: Said he was proud to host at the seat of his institution a workshop on a school subject that is nothing less than the key to teaching and learning, and that mastery of reading is essential in primary school. To this end, he stressed in his address, it is essential to make parents or guardians of pupils aware of the crucial importance for learners of knowing how to read and understand texts.

a1355.speaker: Abdillahi Omar, coordinator of the literacy programme at the National Union of Djiboutian Women (UNFD)
a1355.name: Abdillahi Omar
a1355.title: coordinator of the literacy programme at the National Union of Djiboutian Women (UNFD)
a1355.speech: Recalled the divine injunction given to the Prophet of Islam at the very beginning of his revelation: "Read, read, read in the name of the GOOD LORD" — a fine way of proclaiming the greatness, for a human being, of knowing how to read through religious texts. He recalled the two strands that this component seeks to improve: pupils' reading performance in basic education from the 1st to the 5th year in the country, through the involvement of community organisations such as parents' associations and school management committees.

a1355.speaker: Ahmed Hamadou Ibrahim, regional inspector and head of service of the Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training (MENFOP)
a1355.name: Ahmed Hamadou Ibrahim
a1355.title: regional inspector and head of service of the Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training (MENFOP)
a1355.speech: Said he was enthusiastic about witnessing the assistance of public education partners in a field that is essential to learning and teaching. Reading is the key to learning well; it is a means for schoolchildren to learn. Involving pupils' guardians is a strategy that will certainly strengthen mastery of knowing how to read and understand.

a1355.speaker: Head teachers of the basic schools
a1355.name: Head teachers of the basic schools
a1355.speech: Set out the reading-strengthening activities implemented since the beginning of the current school year, including support classes scheduled outside normal class hours, each school putting in place extra hours of support classes for children with learning difficulties.

a1428.speaker: Sahle-Work Zewde, President of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
a1428.name: Sahle-Work Zewde
a1428.title: President of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
a1428.speech: Welcomed the efforts undertaken to further strengthen the unique, long-standing relations between the peoples of Ethiopia and Djibouti, while receiving the delegation from Djibouti made up of Djiboutian diplomats, former Ethio-Djibouti Railway staff and young Ethiopians born in Djibouti; during the meeting, stressed the need to intensify collective efforts in the areas of public diplomacy in order to further maximise the untapped opportunities in the fields of culture, tourism and history.

a1428.speaker: Members of the Djiboutian delegation
a1428.name: Members of the Djiboutian delegation
a1428.speech: After a warm welcome, expressed their deep gratitude for the warm reception given to them.

a1428.speaker: A former Ethio-Djibouti Railway official (anonymous)
a1428.name: A former Ethio-Djibouti Railway official (anonymous)
a1428.speech: Nicknaming the century-old railway an "umbilical cord" that links the two brotherly peoples, insisted on the need to speed up the creation of the former Ethio-Djibouti Railway staff associations in order to further invigorate the historical ties.

a1589.speaker: National Office of Civil Protection (ONPC), Côte d'Ivoire, Facebook post
a1589.name: National Office of Civil Protection (ONPC)
a1589.title: Côte d'Ivoire, Facebook post
a1589.speech: "Collision between two 24-seat minibuses at Ahizabré, a village located about 20 kilometres from Gagnoa, on the Gagnoa-Soubré road. Provisional toll: 31 victims, including 20 deaths confirmed by the nurse of the said village's health centre," the ONPC said in a post on Facebook.

a1589.speaker: National Office of Civil Protection (ONPC), Côte d'Ivoire
a1589.name: National Office of Civil Protection (ONPC)
a1589.title: Côte d'Ivoire
a1589.speech: According to the ONPC, the accident occurred at night around 7:30 p.m. (GMT and local time) and the rescue operation by the region's firefighters is "finished".

a1589.speaker: Ministry of Transport (Côte d'Ivoire)
a1589.name: Ministry of Transport (Côte d'Ivoire)
a1589.speech: Between 1,000 and 1,500 people are killed on average each year on the roads of Côte d'Ivoire, according to the Ministry of Transport, for 1.5 million vehicles in circulation.

a1797.speaker: International Monetary Fund, World Economic Outlook Statistical Appendix (April 2025)
a1797.name: International Monetary Fund
a1797.title: World Economic Outlook Statistical Appendix (April 2025)
a1797.speech: Cited as the source for the review's findings: every EAC country is classified as a net debtor by the IMF, meaning their external liabilities exceed their foreign assets; Tanzania is projected to grow by 5.4 per cent in 2025; Kenya faces a current account deficit projected at 5.1 per cent of GDP in 2025 and Tanzania a deficit of 3.2 per cent of GDP; global interest rates are projected to average 4.2 per cent in the United States this year.

a1797.speaker: World Bank
a1797.name: World Bank
a1797.speech: According to the World Bank, meeting East Africa's infrastructure requirements sustainably would demand annual investments equivalent to about 5 per cent of GDP.

a1809.speaker: Fassou Théa, Guinean Minister of Fisheries and the Maritime Economy
a1809.name: Fassou Théa
a1809.title: Guinean Minister of Fisheries and the Maritime Economy
a1809.speech: Set out his vision for the fisheries sector in Guinea, a strategic but still under-exploited field according to him, insisting on his ambition to popularise artisanal and industrial fishing in order to make it a lever of growth and of the fight against poverty: "Guinea has one of the greatest fisheries potentials in West Africa. Yet a good part of our population does not yet profit from it. My department is committed to putting in place the necessary means so that fishing is no longer perceived as a marginal activity, but as a pillar of local development." ; announced the establishment of training programmes for young people, the development of local fish processing units and the creation of marketing hubs to facilitate the distribution of fishery products in all regions, including in the interior of the country; mentioned projects to equip artisanal fishermen, strengthen the cold chain and encourage local cooperatives, alongside the modernisation of port infrastructure.

a1809.speaker: Fassou Théa, Guinean Minister of Fisheries and the Maritime Economy
a1809.name: Fassou Théa
a1809.title: Guinean Minister of Fisheries and the Maritime Economy
a1809.speech: Recalled the importance of unity and stability in order to make these ambitions a reality: "Let us preserve peace and work together. It is in a serene climate that we will be able to build a Guinea where fishing and the maritime economy will benefit everyone," he concluded.

a1889.speaker: Motorcycle taxi driver in Juba (unnamed)
a1889.name: Motorcycle taxi driver in Juba (unnamed)
a1889.speech: “That's too far,” said the motorcycle taxi, before charging me double to get there.

a1889.speaker: Ian Alsworth-Elvey, Managing Director, SABMiller/South Sudan Beverages Limited
a1889.name: Ian Alsworth-Elvey
a1889.title: Managing Director, SABMiller/South Sudan Beverages Limited
a1889.speech: “The cost of doing business here is high,” Alsworth-Elvey told Daily Maverick ; “But, the returns are commensurate.”

a1889.speaker: Ian Alsworth-Elvey, Managing Director, SABMiller/South Sudan Beverages Limited
a1889.name: Ian Alsworth-Elvey
a1889.title: Managing Director, SABMiller/South Sudan Beverages Limited
a1889.speech: “There was no regulatory framework in place in the beginning,” he said ; “This has its pros and cons. It gives you the opportunity to shape the regulations, but it does mean that a lot of things are based on personal relationships.”

a1889.speaker: Ian Alsworth-Elvey, Managing Director, SABMiller/South Sudan Beverages Limited
a1889.name: Ian Alsworth-Elvey
a1889.title: Managing Director, SABMiller/South Sudan Beverages Limited
a1889.speech: Describes the reliance on the Kenyan port of Mombasa as a potential “nightmare”, but one shared by businesses all over East Africa, for which the port is the major and often only connection with international transport networks.

a1889.speaker: Ian Alsworth-Elvey, Managing Director, SABMiller/South Sudan Beverages Limited
a1889.name: Ian Alsworth-Elvey
a1889.title: Managing Director, SABMiller/South Sudan Beverages Limited
a1889.speech: “We've had to recruit staff out of a labour pool that has never been formally employed,” said Alsworth-Elvey. “The encouraging part is that it improves all the time.” ; on distribution via the Nile waterways: “Big business looks to find alternative solutions, and then we become the trend-setters. If we can deliver beer on the water systems, then food will inevitably follow.”

a1889.speaker: Richard, barman at a local pub near the brewery in Juba
a1889.name: Richard
a1889.title: barman at a local pub near the brewery in Juba
a1889.speech: “The taste changes. I don't know what they are doing up in that factory – they adding this, adding that. You don't know what it will be. But it is still my favourite. It is from South Sudan. It is ours.”

a1949.speaker: Souleiman Elmi, President of the Association of Young People of the Château d’eau neighbourhood (AJCD)
a1949.name: Souleiman Elmi
a1949.title: President of the Association of Young People of the Château d’eau neighbourhood (AJCD)
a1949.speech: Announced that “Our main objective is to count the families living in this sector. This survey is particularly important for several reasons. First, it will allow us to identify by name the households living in this sector. Second, this information will help us to set up our project to improve access to water in your sector.”

a1949.speaker: Survey leaders / surveyors of the AJCD
a1949.name: Survey leaders / surveyors of the AJCD
a1949.speech: Urged the mothers of families to cooperate with the association’s surveyors by providing only accurate and truthful data, informed them that each of their answers is crucial to the success of the survey, and encouraged them to answer honestly by giving accurate and detailed responses.

a2124.speaker: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda, Minister of Health of Malawi
a2124.name: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda
a2124.title: Minister of Health of Malawi
a2124.speech: Says Malawi has sufficient drug stocks to manage HIV and Aids for the next 11 months, allaying fears that the suspension of USAid funding could derail progress: "We have continued to provide services as usual. Where USAid has withdrawn staff, we have put our own health workers to fill the gaps. The most important thing is that we have sufficient stocks for managing HIV and Aids to cover us for at least eleven months - nearly a year from now."

a2124.speaker: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda, Minister of Health of Malawi
a2124.name: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda
a2124.title: Minister of Health of Malawi
a2124.speech: Said the Malawi Government is also leveraging the Health Sector Joint Fund supported by contributions from Germany, Norway and the United Kingdom to bridge the financial gap left by USAid funding, and urged the public not to panic, adding that the government is engaging with other partners to ensure continuity in the health sector.

a2124.speaker: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda, Minister of Health of Malawi
a2124.name: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda
a2124.title: Minister of Health of Malawi
a2124.speech: Did not provide specific details on how the government sourced the additional healthcare workers to replace those supported by the US Government funding.

a2124.speaker: East, Central and Southern Africa Health Community (ECSA-HC) conference
a2124.name: East
a2124.title: Central and Southern Africa Health Community (ECSA-HC) conference
a2124.speech: Played down the potential impact of USAid funding suspension, citing its cost-effective operational model.

a2124.speaker: Sibusiso Sibandze, acting director general of ECSA-HC
a2124.name: Sibusiso Sibandze
a2124.title: acting director general of ECSA-HC
a2124.speech: Said the organisation maximises the value of every dollar received: "While USAid funding has been crucial, we implement our activities in a cost-effective manner. Even with the funding withdrawal, we are confident in our ability to continue supporting member States."

a2124.speaker: Michael Usi, Vice-President of Malawi
a2124.name: Michael Usi
a2124.title: Vice-President of Malawi
a2124.speech: Urged member States to prioritise health data integration and innovative financing strategies to strengthen regional health systems.

a2173.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency (Doge) and CEO of SpaceX and Tesla (post on X)
a2173.name: Elon Musk
a2173.title: head of the Department of Government Efficiency (Doge) and CEO of SpaceX and Tesla (post on X)
a2173.speech: has said he is leaving the Trump administration and thanked Trump for the opportunity to help run the Department of Government Efficiency: "As my scheduled time as a Special Government Employee comes to an end, I would like to thank President @realDonaldTrump for the opportunity to reduce wasteful spending" ; "The @DOGE mission will only strengthen over time as it becomes a way of life throughout the government."

a2173.speaker: Elon Musk (interview with CBS)
a2173.name: Elon Musk (interview with CBS)
a2173.speech: said he was "disappointed" with Trump's budget bill, which proposes multi-trillion dollar tax breaks and a boost to defence spending, saying the "big, beautiful bill" would increase the federal deficit; also said he thought it "undermines the work" of Doge ; "I think a bill can be big or it could be beautiful. But I don't know if it could be both."

a2173.speaker: Elon Musk
a2173.name: Elon Musk
a2173.speech: initially pledged to cut "at least $2 trillion" from the federal government budget, before halving this target, then reducing it to $150bn.

a2173.speaker: Elon Musk
a2173.name: Elon Musk
a2173.speech: announced in late April that he would step back to run his companies again after becoming a lightning rod for criticism of Trump's efforts to shake up Washington.

a2173.speaker: Elon Musk (speaking to the Washington Post in Texas)
a2173.name: Elon Musk (speaking to the Washington Post in Texas)
a2173.speech: "Doge is just becoming the whipping boy for everything." ; "Something bad would happen anywhere, and we would get blamed for it even if we had nothing to do with it."

a2173.speaker: Tesla
a2173.name: Tesla
a2173.speech: recently warned investors that the financial pain could continue, declining to offer a growth forecast while saying "changing political sentiment" could meaningfully hurt demand for the vehicles.

a2173.speaker: Elon Musk (earnings call with investors)
a2173.name: Elon Musk (earnings call with investors)
a2173.speech: told investors that the time he allocates to Doge "will drop significantly" and that he would be "allocating far more of my time to Tesla."

a2173.speaker: Pam Bondi, US Attorney General
a2173.name: Pam Bondi
a2173.title: US Attorney General
a2173.speech: warned her office would treat acts of vandalism against Tesla as "domestic terrorism."

a2173.speaker: Elon Musk (speaking at an economic forum in Doha, Qatar)
a2173.name: Elon Musk (speaking at an economic forum in Doha
a2173.title: Qatar)
a2173.speech: said he was committed to being the leader of Tesla for the next five years.

a2173.speaker: Elon Musk
a2173.name: Elon Musk
a2173.speech: said earlier this month he would cut back his political donations after spending nearly $300m to back Trump's presidential campaign and other Republicans last year.

a2257.speaker: John Siafa, Monrovia City Mayor
a2257.name: John Siafa
a2257.title: Monrovia City Mayor
a2257.speech: Charged citizens to forge transformative approaches that will enhance sanitation in Monrovia and its environs: "It is about time that citizens collaborate with the Monrovia City Corporation (MCC) in ensuring that the city remains clean and green at all times." According to him, waste disposal, especially in the principal streets across the country, continues to hinder the progress of sanitation in Liberia ; says he remains committed to restoring the dignity of the country's capital.

a2257.speaker: Jerolinmek Piah, Information Minister of Liberia
a2257.name: Jerolinmek Piah
a2257.title: Information Minister of Liberia
a2257.speech: Says the Liberian Government recognizes the present challenges confronting the City of Monrovia and its residents. Minister Piah named the management of huge waste, urban congestion, and inadequate infrastructure, among others, indicating that those challenges can be addressed through collaborative efforts. He noted that the Monrovia that was inherited under the current government will be transformed in the coming years for future generations, and Liberians must work to build a cleaner, safer, and more prosperous Monrovia for all.

a2284.speaker: Madi Jobarteh, human rights activist (training facilitator)
a2284.name: Madi Jobarteh
a2284.title: human rights activist (training facilitator)
a2284.speech: Emphasized that as a civil society organization, they are accountable to the people first and foremost, and urged GYIN-Gambia to demonstrate transparency and accountability in all its operations.

a2284.speaker: Modou S. Joof, GYIN-Gambia's Board Chairperson
a2284.name: Modou S. Joof
a2284.title: GYIN-Gambia's Board Chairperson
a2284.speech: Said they have established higher standards for board operations and have strengthened GYIN-Gambia by clarifying their role in supporting the organization's development. The training, he said, aligns with GYIN-Gambia's commitment to youth development and to creating sustainable socio-economic opportunities.

a2284.speaker: Mamadou Edrisa Nije, Executive Director of GYIN-Gambia
a2284.name: Mamadou Edrisa Nije
a2284.title: Executive Director of GYIN-Gambia
a2284.speech: Said with Freedom House's assistance, they have achieved a better structure, noting that the training will ensure an effective board to drive "our mission forward."

a2295.speaker: Save the Children
a2295.name: Save the Children
a2295.speech: yesterday said it had witnessed a "horrifying" spike in the number of children being sexually assaulted in DR Congo, recording more than triple the number compared to a year ago. ; Save the Children recorded over 478 cases of gender-based violence (GBV) between January and June - an increase of 249% compared to last year. It said 172 of the incidents, most of them rape cases, were against children.

a2295.speaker: 16-year-old Congolese girl (refugee in Burundi, anonymous)
a2295.name: 16-year-old Congolese girl (refugee in Burundi
a2295.title: anonymous)
a2295.speech: "Armed men entered our house and raped me, my sister and my mother." ; "It is very hard to look my mother in eye after what happened, but also very difficult for our mother to talk to us about it."

a2295.speaker: Nadege Nizigama, Save the Children's child protection and GBV case worker for Burundi
a2295.name: Nadege Nizigama
a2295.title: Save the Children's child protection and GBV case worker for Burundi
a2295.speech: "For the last few months, I have heard horrifying stories of children being raped together with their parents, and mothers being raped in front of their children."

a2295.speaker: Geoffrey Kirenga, Save the Children's Burundi head
a2295.name: Geoffrey Kirenga
a2295.title: Save the Children's Burundi head
a2295.speech: "Tragically we know the number of cases we have registered is just a drop in the ocean."

a2295.speaker: Geoffrey Kirenga, Save the Children's Burundi head
a2295.name: Geoffrey Kirenga
a2295.title: Save the Children's Burundi head
a2295.speech: "The funding gaps we're now facing could force us to close down programmes that are a lifeline to children and families in dire need."

a2317.speaker: Message sent to senior USAID officials recounting Saturday’s events (described to Bloomberg News by four people familiar with it)
a2317.name: Message sent to senior USAID officials recounting Saturday’s events (described to Bloomberg News by four people familiar with it)
a2317.speech: recounted that the DOGE team had been seeking information from the more than 60-year-old foreign-aid agency’s officials for several days and they weren’t taking no for an answer; it described a confrontation between the DOGE workers and a security official at USAID who refused the Musk aides’ request to enter a highly secure room, and said the DOGE employees visited several floors and went from office to office, searching desks ; according to descriptions of the message, the DOGE team included Luke Farritor, Edward Coristine, Jeremy Lewin and Gavin Kliger.

a2317.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a2317.name: Elon Musk
a2317.title: head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a2317.speech: informed the agency’s security officials, in a call from one of the DOGE employees, that he would involve the US Marshals Service if his team wasn’t given access to even sensitive information.

a2317.speaker: Katie Miller, attached by Trump to DOGE (post on X)
a2317.name: Katie Miller
a2317.title: attached by Trump to DOGE (post on X)
a2317.speech: "No classified material was accessed without proper security clearances," wrote Katie Miller in a post on X Sunday ; She didn’t respond to a request for comment sent to her LinkedIn account.

a2317.speaker: People familiar with the documents (anonymous)
a2317.name: People familiar with the documents (anonymous)
a2317.speech: said that while the personnel documents the DOGE team was seeking are not classified, entry to the SCIF requires a top secret/sensitive compartmented information security clearance.

a2317.speaker: Gavin Kliger, DOGE team member and adviser to the director of the Office of Personnel Management (Substack post)
a2317.name: Gavin Kliger
a2317.title: DOGE team member and adviser to the director of the Office of Personnel Management (Substack post)
a2317.speech: "The real story — the truth about Matt Gaetz’s rise and fall — is a byzantine tale of international intrigue, deep state machinations, and the awesome power of America’s permanent bureaucracy to destroy its enemies," Kliger wrote.

a2317.speaker: DOGE team members
a2317.name: DOGE team members
a2317.speech: None of the DOGE team members responded to requests for comment sent to email accounts that they were assigned by USAID officials.

a2317.speaker: Project 2025 document, a plan from the Heritage Foundation
a2317.name: Project 2025 document
a2317.title: a plan from the Heritage Foundation
a2317.speech: said that the agency had become a "platform to pursue overseas a divisive political and cultural agenda that promotes abortion, climate extremism, gender radicalism, and interventions against perceived systemic racism."

a2317.speaker: Five people familiar with the discussions (anonymous)
a2317.name: Five people familiar with the discussions (anonymous)
a2317.speech: said DOGE’s review of the agency began in earnest last week, when the new administration asked detailed questions during meetings about organizational charts, contractors and aid programs, and that meetings centered around obtaining a list of people who work for USAID and preparing memos about moving the agency under the State Department’s foreign assistance bureau; the DOGE team had another task: to collect details from USAID databases about the people who work for the agency and the aid programs they are assigned to, as well as information about when employees logged into computers and used their badges to enter conference rooms.

a2317.speaker: Peter Marocco, former USAID and State Department official
a2317.name: Peter Marocco
a2317.title: former USAID and State Department official
a2317.speech: didn’t immediately respond to a telephone call seeking comment Sunday evening.

a2317.speaker: Nick Gottlieb, USAID’s director of employee and labor relations (email of Jan. 30)
a2317.name: Nick Gottlieb
a2317.title: USAID’s director of employee and labor relations (email of Jan. 30)
a2317.speech: The email carried the subject line, "Farewell and Thanks (Again) – Illegal Activity in the USAID Front Office." It said, "Today, representatives of the Agency’s front office and DOGE instructed me to violate the due process of our employees by issuing immediate termination notices to a group of employees without due process. I refused and have provided Acting Administrator [Jason] Gray with written notification of my refusal." ; Gottlieb’s email also said that moments before he sent it, he was notified that he would be placed on administrative leave.

a2317.speaker: Eight people with direct knowledge of the matter (anonymous)
a2317.name: Eight people with direct knowledge of the matter (anonymous)
a2317.speech: said that the next day the DOGE team worked late into the evening and, with Marocco, took steps to change the agency’s offices — artwork that depicted how USAID supported the LGBTQ community or that contained a mention of diversity, equity and inclusion was removed from the walls, and eventually everything was taken down.

a2317.speaker: Five people with direct knowledge (anonymous)
a2317.name: Five people with direct knowledge (anonymous)
a2317.speech: said tensions had escalated that day because the DOGE team had still failed to secure access to the badging information it wanted from the security office, and that evening USAID chief of staff Matt Hopson resigned and acting administrator Jason Gray also threatened to leave.

a2317.speaker: Matt Hopson, USAID chief of staff, and Jason Gray, USAID acting administrator
a2317.name: Matt Hopson
a2317.title: USAID chief of staff, and Jason Gray, USAID acting administrator
a2317.speech: Neither Hopson nor Gray responded to a request for comment.

a2317.speaker: Elon Musk (post on X)
a2317.name: Elon Musk (post on X)
a2317.speech: "USAID is a criminal organization. Time for it to die," Musk posted on X.

a2317.speaker: USAID mass email to employees
a2317.name: USAID mass email to employees
a2317.speech: On Monday morning, USAID employees received a mass email saying the headquarters would be closed for the day and instructing most of them to work remotely: "Further guidance will be forthcoming," it said.

a2495.speaker: Kathleen Addy, Chairperson of the National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE)
a2495.name: Kathleen Addy
a2495.title: Chairperson of the National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE)
a2495.speech: Has advised citizens, particularly the youth, to vote for candidates based on issues that speak to their conscience and policies they believe will accelerate socio-economic development; urged them to reject politicians who tried to entice them with money, gifts and promises to incite violence and threaten the nation's globally revered peace and stability: "We came here to discuss things like violence and violent activities, and remind citizens that these things are outside of the law, and it doesn't help our country. So, we must avoid becoming victims of politicians who come and give us arms, give us knives, and a little bit of money to go and cause trouble during the election."

a2495.speaker: Kathleen Addy, Chairperson of the National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE)
a2495.name: Kathleen Addy
a2495.title: Chairperson of the National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE)
a2495.speech: Stressed that the NCCE would not relent in its mandate and mission to educate citizens against activities that could potentially disrupt the nation's democracy: "We are doing this work not only here, but in various less endowed communities around the country. We are giving extra attention to those communities because we want the message to sink here very clearly. Because a lot of times it is the young people from these areas that are misused or misled into taking up illegal activities around elections."

a2495.speaker: Kathleen Addy, Chairperson of the National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE)
a2495.name: Kathleen Addy
a2495.title: Chairperson of the National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE)
a2495.speech: Called on law enforcement agencies and other relevant authorities to pursue and prosecute individuals and groups who embarked on activities that tended to create political tensions before, during and after elections, and that "if we all do our mandate, the system will work."

a2495.speaker: Gilbert Sam, Senior Election Specialist of IFES Ghana
a2495.name: Gilbert Sam
a2495.title: Senior Election Specialist of IFES Ghana
a2495.speech: Said his outfit was committed to addressing the issues of inclusion in the nation's political landscape, particularly for women and persons with disabilities.

a2495.speaker: Gilbert Sam, Senior Election Specialist of IFES Ghana
a2495.name: Gilbert Sam
a2495.title: Senior Election Specialist of IFES Ghana
a2495.speech: Said it was intensifying the campaign against vote buying, and stressed that such illicit activities would hamper the country's socio-economic development: "We've been fighting against galamsey for a while now. So imagine a galamseyer funds a certain politician or MP who then finds their way into Parliament. Do you think if there's a bill to tackle the issue, that person would be able to vote in support? No."

a2497.speaker: The Washington Post editorial board
a2497.name: The Washington Post editorial board
a2497.speech: Published a piece on November 24 in which it laid out its views on the arrest warrants for Israeli officials recently issued by the Pre-Trial Chamber of the International Criminal Court (ICC); the article suggests that the ICC has failed to address international crimes in Syria, Myanmar and Sudan.

a2497.speaker: The Washington Post editorial board
a2497.name: The Washington Post editorial board
a2497.speech: Reproduces the talking point that Israel as "a democratic country that is committed to human rights" is capable of investigating its own security forces, and argues that the ICC should not put "elected leaders of a democratic country with its own independent judiciary in the same category as dictators and authoritarians who kill with impunity".

a2497.speaker: The Washington Post editorial board
a2497.name: The Washington Post editorial board
a2497.speech: Claims that the arrest warrants "undermine the ICC's credibility and give credence to accusations of hypocrisy and selective prosecution".

a2497.speaker: Karim Khan, ICC Prosecutor
a2497.name: Karim Khan
a2497.title: ICC Prosecutor
a2497.speech: Asserted that his office is still investigating ongoing crimes in Sudan.

a2497.speaker: ICC Office of the Prosecutor and Pre-Trial Chamber
a2497.name: ICC Office of the Prosecutor and Pre-Trial Chamber
a2497.speech: Concurred that although the crimes of "deportation" and "persecution" were perpetrated by nationals of a non-state party and on the territory of a non-state party (Myanmar), the "conduct" constituting the crimes forced the victims into the territory of a state party (Bangladesh); consequently, the ICC should have jurisdiction because the crimes have been committed "in part" on a territory of a state party.

a2497.speaker: ICC decision in the case of Ivory Coast first lady Simone Gbagbo
a2497.name: ICC decision in the case of Ivory Coast first lady Simone Gbagbo
a2497.speech: Laid out that the law of the ICC allows it to intervene if the "investigative activities undertaken by the domestic authorities are not tangible, concrete and progressive".

a2497.speaker: 2014 UN Commission of Inquiry (report)
a2497.name: 2014 UN Commission of Inquiry (report)
a2497.speech: Addressed the "procedural, structural and substantive shortcomings, which continue to compromise Israel's ability to adequately fulfil its duty to investigate".

a2497.speaker: Palestinian and Israeli NGOs
a2497.name: Palestinian and Israeli NGOs
a2497.speech: Have repeatedly scrutinised Israel's tendency to whitewash its own crimes.

a2497.speaker: Amnesty International
a2497.name: Amnesty International
a2497.speech: Considered "an ICC investigation [to be] the only way" to uphold international law.

a2497.speaker: Human Rights Watch
a2497.name: Human Rights Watch
a2497.speech: Has documented Israel's failure to prosecute war crimes as far back as the 2014 war on Gaza, the second Intifada, the first Intifada and even the Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 1982.

a2497.speaker: Valentina Azarova, Triestino Mariniello and Abdelghany Sayed (two previously published articles)
a2497.name: Valentina Azarova
a2497.title: Triestino Mariniello and Abdelghany Sayed (two previously published articles)
a2497.speech: Have previously argued that the court's action on crimes committed against Palestinians could help it redress its problems with effectiveness and legitimacy.

a2497.speaker: +972 Magazine, the Local Call and The Guardian (investigation)
a2497.name: +972 Magazine
a2497.title: the Local Call and The Guardian (investigation)
a2497.speech: Revealed in May that Israel ran a nine-year, state-orchestrated espionage and intimidation campaign against the ICC to shield its nationals from prosecution.

a2624.speaker: Joseph Nye, international relations scholar
a2624.name: Joseph Nye
a2624.title: international relations scholar
a2624.speech: His concept of hard and soft power offers a strong framework for understanding how nations behave and interact in their pursuit of objectives; he proposed that the most effective strategy for states today is a combination of both hard power and soft power, known as “smart power”.

a2713.speaker: Imam Alhagie Muhammed Lamin Touray, former President of The Gambia's Supreme Islamic Council
a2713.name: Imam Alhagie Muhammed Lamin Touray
a2713.title: former President of The Gambia's Supreme Islamic Council
a2713.speech: In his sermon, he preached peace, unity, and stability, and urged Muslims to fulfil their religious obligations with dedication.

a2713.speaker: Imam Alhagie Muhammed Lamin Touray
a2713.name: Imam Alhagie Muhammed Lamin Touray
a2713.speech: expressed profound gratitude to President Barrow for sponsoring the construction, recalled past challenges the community faced in raising funds for a mosque, and said the President had fulfilled their long-held dream. "This singular act will enhance the spiritual development of the community." He also thanked women, youth, and religious leaders for their support during the project.

a2713.speaker: Chief Falalo Touray and Alkalo Dembo Darboe of Gunjur
a2713.name: Chief Falalo Touray and Alkalo Dembo Darboe of Gunjur
a2713.speech: commended the President, noted that the mosque, together with ongoing road and infrastructure projects, will promote the religious and social development of Gunjur, and urged residents to support the President to enable him to continue his development agenda.

a2713.speaker: Hamat N.K. Bah, Minister of Regional Government, Lands and Religious Affairs
a2713.name: Hamat N.K. Bah
a2713.title: Minister of Regional Government, Lands and Religious Affairs
a2713.speech: described the mosque as one of the most modern in the country, built to meet contemporary architectural standards, and disclosed that President Barrow has funded several mosque projects nationwide, reflecting his commitment to Islam and the spiritual development of Muslims.

a2713.speaker: Hamat N.K. Bah, Minister of Regional Government, Lands and Religious Affairs
a2713.name: Hamat N.K. Bah
a2713.title: Minister of Regional Government, Lands and Religious Affairs
a2713.speech: echoed calls for Gambians to support the President's re-election bid in December, thanked elders and religious leaders for preaching peace and tolerance, and urged them to continue guiding to preserve national tranquillity.

a2713.speaker: President Adama Barrow
a2713.name: President Adama Barrow
a2713.speech: In his inaugural statement, thanked the Gunjur community for the honour, noting he had long pledged to support the project; described Gunjur as a historic Islamic settlement that produced renowned scholars including Omar Bun Jeng and Hatab Bojang; said mosques play a vital role in the spiritual and moral development of society; thanked anonymous donors who supported the construction and urged the community to pray for them; called the mosque a progressive project that has changed the infrastructural landscape of Gunjur; challenged residents to take good care of the mosque and its facilities, and pledged government support for its upkeep and maintenance.

a2713.speaker: President Adama Barrow
a2713.name: President Adama Barrow
a2713.speech: On the upcoming December elections, urged Gambians to pray for peace and reassured the nation of the government's commitment to a smooth and credible process. "There are no losers in elections. A peaceful and credible process promotes The Gambia's image as a democratic country."

a2713.speaker: Gabonese and Turkish contractors
a2713.name: Gabonese and Turkish contractors
a2713.speech: briefed the President on the progress of the twisting tower and related infrastructure; the project is expected to be ready for inauguration next year.

a2713.speaker: Saikou Dukureh, Consul General
a2713.name: Saikou Dukureh
a2713.title: Consul General
a2713.speech: welcomed the President and thanked him for the engagement; described Gambians in Gabon as hardworking, united, and law-abiding, and commended the government for supporting their welfare.

a2713.speaker: Jakarta Dampha, community representative
a2713.name: Jakarta Dampha
a2713.title: community representative
a2713.speech: said there has been marked improvement in the well-being of Gambians in Gabon since President Barrow took office, and noted that the President's leadership has ensured that Gambians in the diaspora are not discriminated against and that their concerns are addressed promptly.

a2713.speaker: Hawa Dukureh, speaking on behalf of the youth
a2713.name: Hawa Dukureh
a2713.title: speaking on behalf of the youth
a2713.speech: commended the President for dispatching a team of immigration officials to issue national documents, said nearly 200 people were processed, but appealed for support to ensure the passports are delivered.

a2713.speaker: President Adama Barrow
a2713.name: President Adama Barrow
a2713.speech: expressed gratitude for the warm reception at the airport, which he said even impressed his host, President Oligui Nguema; said dialogue is key to national unity and described it as a great honour to serve as Chief Guest of Honour at Gabon's Independence Anniversary.

a2713.speaker: President Adama Barrow
a2713.name: President Adama Barrow
a2713.speech: On diaspora support, reaffirmed his government's commitment to assisting Gambians abroad, said the decision to send immigration officials to Gabon was to ensure citizens have access to documents, and pledged to prioritise the delivery of all processed passports upon his return to Banjul. He also advised Gambians seeking repatriation to apply through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for a smooth process.

a2713.speaker: President Adama Barrow
a2713.name: President Adama Barrow
a2713.speech: said the government has laid the foundation stone for 1,500 km of roads across the country and highlighted progress in electricity, health, transport, and education; encouraged those with voter cards to exercise their right, and urged those without to encourage family and friends to vote for continuity; urged the community to maintain unity, peace, and respect for lawful authority.

a2713.speaker: Dr Ahmadou Lamin Samateh, Minister of Health
a2713.name: Dr Ahmadou Lamin Samateh
a2713.title: Minister of Health
a2713.speech: described the Buduk health post as "another significant milestone", reflecting the government's commitment to improving healthcare services.

a2713.speaker: President Adama Barrow
a2713.name: President Adama Barrow
a2713.speech: said the opening of the health post aligns with his administration's broader goal of ensuring access to quality healthcare for all Gambians.

a2713.speaker: President Adama Barrow
a2713.name: President Adama Barrow
a2713.speech: Speaking on board the ferry, said the tour reflects his government's strategy of delivering social projects directly to ordinary Gambians. "Infrastructure is the foundation upon which all other sectors rely," describing it as a key pillar of his development agenda.

a2713.speaker: Communities in the North Bank Region (residents)
a2713.name: Communities in the North Bank Region (residents)
a2713.speech: expressed joy over the projects, saying the new roads will open access to markets and improve delivery of social services such as schools and health facilities.

a2713.speaker: A resident (unnamed), Fass Njaga Choi
a2713.name: A resident (unnamed)
a2713.title: Fass Njaga Choi
a2713.speech: "This road has been our dream for years. We thank the President for remembering us."

a2713.speaker: Alhaji Kala Darboe
a2713.name: Alhaji Kala Darboe
a2713.speech: said the new road will create opportunities for women and farmers, while improving access to education, healthcare, and other essential services.

a2713.speaker: Lamin Saidykhan, North Bank Region Governor
a2713.name: Lamin Saidykhan
a2713.title: North Bank Region Governor
a2713.speech: commended the government for what he described as unprecedented development that has transformed livelihoods in the area, and urged residents to reflect on the impact of these projects on ordinary people.

a2713.speaker: The National Assembly Member for Upper Badibou
a2713.name: The National Assembly Member for Upper Badibou
a2713.speech: described the gathering as significant, noting ongoing support for the President in Badibou, attributing this to the government's track record of delivering roads and health centres, and adding that previous administrations had failed to construct the road despite strong local support.

a2713.speaker: Alhaji Jagne, Chief of Central Badibou, and Councillor Maimuna Bah
a2713.name: Alhaji Jagne
a2713.title: Chief of Central Badibou, and Councillor Maimuna Bah
a2713.speech: expressed gratitude to the President, recalled past difficulties accessing health facilities due to poor roads, and said patients can now reach care within minutes thanks to the new road, health centre, and provision of ambulances.

a2713.speaker: Fatou Kinteh, Minister of Gender and Children's Welfare
a2713.name: Fatou Kinteh
a2713.title: Minister of Gender and Children's Welfare
a2713.speech: said President Barrow's development agenda is visible across all sectors, particularly in women's empowerment; noted that women now hold influential positions in government and called on women to support the President, adding that Gambian women have pledged to contribute to his nomination fees in December.

a2713.speaker: Sulayman Sumareh, Managing Director of the National Roads Authority
a2713.name: Sulayman Sumareh
a2713.title: Managing Director of the National Roads Authority
a2713.speech: disclosed that the Salikenni-Njaba Kunda road is fully government-funded and said the project will improve connectivity and enhance access to health, education, and other social services.

a2713.speaker: President Adama Barrow
a2713.name: President Adama Barrow
a2713.speech: described the new road as part of his government's plan to connect all communities across the country. "The North Bank Region has received unprecedented attention under this government with the construction of several roads." He reassured citizens of his administration's commitment to infrastructure and urged communities to take ownership and maintain the projects to serve their intended purpose.
