a2713.speaker: Kebba Jallow, former leader of the People's Progressive Party (PPP)
a2713.name: Kebba Jallow
a2713.title: former leader of the People's Progressive Party (PPP)
a2713.speech: reaffirmed his support for President Barrow, saying the President has done so much for the country and deserves another term in office; the delegation pledged to support the President's candidature and work to ensure victory in the December 5th presidential election.

a2713.speaker: Seedy S.K. Njie, Deputy Public Relations Officer of the NPP
a2713.name: Seedy S.K. Njie
a2713.title: Deputy Public Relations Officer of the NPP
a2713.speech: welcomed the PPP executives into the Alliance and said President Barrow is pleased to accept the endorsement.

a2713.speaker: Gibril Faal, Chief Executive Officer of GK Partners
a2713.name: Gibril Faal
a2713.title: Chief Executive Officer of GK Partners
a2713.speech: briefed the President on the activities of GK Partners, particularly its ongoing Diaspora Fellowship project being implemented jointly with the International Organisation for Migration (IOM), and updated the President on strides made in diaspora direct investment, noting that The Gambia now leads in monitoring remittance data through the Central Bank of The Gambia.

a2713.speaker: President Adama Barrow
a2713.name: President Adama Barrow
a2713.speech: underscored his commitment to supporting the Diaspora Fellowship project and urged GK Partners to do more public relations work to inform Gambians about their initiatives.

a2843.speaker: Abdirizak Omar Mohamed, Somalia's recently dismissed Minister of Petroleum and Minerals
a2843.name: Abdirizak Omar Mohamed
a2843.title: Somalia's recently dismissed Minister of Petroleum and Minerals
a2843.speech: has linked his removal to disagreements with President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud over addressing long-standing grievances from Hiiraan residents toward the Hirshabelle administration ; revealed that the policy rift centred on how to resolve Hiiraan's complaints, which have persisted since Hirshabelle's formation during President Hassan Sheikh's first term.

a2843.speaker: Abdirizak Omar Mohamed, Somalia's recently dismissed Minister of Petroleum and Minerals
a2843.name: Abdirizak Omar Mohamed
a2843.title: Somalia's recently dismissed Minister of Petroleum and Minerals
a2843.speech: stressed the legitimacy of Hiiraan's grievances, saying they required a collaborative resolution: "In principle, the President, I, and other politicians agreed that the grievances of the people of Hiiraan were legitimate and required resolution, involving both the Hirshabelle administration and the federal government" ; emphasized reconciliation as the cornerstone of his approach, advocating for engaging traditional elders, religious leaders, and local politicians to address foundational issues, including the regional capital and parliamentary representation: "They should collectively decide on the future structure of Hirshabelle and address the core issues underlying the grievances, including the capital city and the composition of Hirshabelle's parliament."

a2843.speaker: Abdirizak Omar Mohamed, Somalia's recently dismissed Minister of Petroleum and Minerals
a2843.name: Abdirizak Omar Mohamed
a2843.title: Somalia's recently dismissed Minister of Petroleum and Minerals
a2843.speech: Despite his dismissal, thanked President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre for the opportunity to serve, and praised the Prime Minister's leadership, which he described as inclusive and rooted in mutual respect: "I remain committed to Somalia's progress, particularly in addressing the needs of Hirshabelle's communities."

a2843.speaker: Abdirizak Omar Mohamed, Somalia's Minister of Petroleum and Minerals
a2843.name: Abdirizak Omar Mohamed
a2843.title: Somalia's Minister of Petroleum and Minerals
a2843.speech: At a 2024 energy conference, emphasized that Somalia's energy resources could drive economic development, create jobs, and reduce reliance on foreign aid if managed responsibly.

a2843.speaker: U.S. Department of Commerce (estimate)
a2843.name: U.S. Department of Commerce (estimate)
a2843.speech: estimated Somalia's untapped oil and gas reserves at 30 billion barrels.

a2854.speaker: Gilberto Silva, Cabo Verdean minister (responsible for water)
a2854.name: Gilberto Silva
a2854.title: Cabo Verdean minister (responsible for water)
a2854.speech: Said in the debate on water supply that a breakdown had caused difficulties in supply, leaving families living without water for weeks in the capital ; said that Electra restored production two days ago with three desalination plants and that the distribution company Águas de Santiago (AdS) guaranteed this would allow supply to be normalised in the coming days ; “The Government has already decided on the implementation of contingency measures that will allow an increase, in the coming months, of about a further 3,200 cubic metres of water per day” ; added that the process of “deep maintenance” of the desalination plants will be accelerated, along with the reduction of losses through the ongoing water-efficiency programme, with interventions budgeted at 500 million escudos (4.5 million euros) ; announced other “structural measures”, such as investments to mobilise a further 15,000 cubic metres of water per day and other network infrastructure in Praia, the contracting of which is being negotiated.

a2854.speaker: Águas de Santiago (AdS)
a2854.name: Águas de Santiago (AdS)
a2854.speech: Guaranteed that the restoration of production by Electra with three desalination plants would make it possible to normalise supply in the coming days.

a2854.speaker: Nilton Duarte, president of Águas de Santiago (AdS)
a2854.name: Nilton Duarte
a2854.title: president of Águas de Santiago (AdS)
a2854.speech: Speaking to Lusa, said that Electra was delivering 12,000 tonnes of water, but that about 15,000 per day are needed to meet the needs of the country’s capital.

a3001.speaker: Abdoulaye Maiga, Prime Minister of Mali (Major General)
a3001.name: Abdoulaye Maiga
a3001.title: Prime Minister of Mali (Major General)
a3001.speech: Underlined the importance of the sixth monthly public-private consultation meeting for responding to the concerns of economic and social actors ; "Our objective is to forge a fruitful partnership between the public and private sectors for an effective handling of the concerns of each stakeholder" ; welcomed the commitment of the participants, noting that their massive turnout testifies to "the growing interest in the new dynamic that has been created."

a3001.speaker: Abdoulaye Maiga, Prime Minister of Mali
a3001.name: Abdoulaye Maiga
a3001.title: Prime Minister of Mali
a3001.speech: Called for this dynamic to be maintained in order to reach the objectives set by the President of the Transition, Army General Assimi Goita, particularly in meeting basic needs and easing the social climate ; "I urge you to conduct an in-depth examination and to hold open debates, in a spirit of brotherhood and mutual respect," stressing the importance of sustainable, poverty-reducing economic growth ; renewed his call to private sector actors to guarantee the supply of essential goods and quality agricultural inputs and to facilitate the free movement of people and goods within the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) ; concluded by welcoming the unanimous adoption by the National Transition Council of the Government's Action Plan 2025-2026.

a3001.speaker: Moussa Alassane Diallo, Minister of Industry and Trade of Mali
a3001.name: Moussa Alassane Diallo
a3001.title: Minister of Industry and Trade of Mali
a3001.speech: Highlighted the obstacles to investment, particularly the high cost of electricity and the shortcomings of basic infrastructure ; "The cost of electricity blows up the operating costs of factories, which often run on generators" ; illustrated his point with the example of the cement sector, where bringing the price per tonne below 90,000 CFA francs would endanger production units ; "Without basic infrastructure and structural reforms, it will be very complicated to attract investment."

a3001.speaker: Moussa Alassane Diallo, Minister of Industry and Trade of Mali
a3001.name: Moussa Alassane Diallo
a3001.title: Minister of Industry and Trade of Mali
a3001.speech: Insisted on the need for structural reforms to improve the business climate, strengthen the productive base and encourage investment ; "These reforms, proposed by the private sector and incorporated into a matrix, will make it possible to consolidate the economy for Mali's emergence over the next five to ten years" ; also mentioned sovereign measures, such as the ban on exporting certain agricultural raw materials (groundnuts, soya, sesame) in order to guarantee their availability to local industries.

a3001.speaker: Moassadeck Bally, president of the National Council of Malian Employers (CNPM)
a3001.name: Moassadeck Bally
a3001.title: president of the National Council of Malian Employers (CNPM)
a3001.speech: Agreed, pointing to the lack of energy as a major obstacle ; "Some investors, such as Diamond Ciment Mali, are switching to solar, but clinker kilns cannot operate that way," expressing his doubts about a fall in cement prices given these constraints.

a3030.speaker: Jefferson T. Koijee, Ex-Mayor of Monrovia and CDC National Secretary General (letter to President Trump)
a3030.name: Jefferson T. Koijee
a3030.title: Ex-Mayor of Monrovia and CDC National Secretary General (letter to President Trump)
a3030.speech: Writes to U.S. President Donald Trump calling on him to stand with the people of Liberia in tackling corruption, human rights violations, and democratic erosion.

a3030.speaker: Jefferson T. Koijee, Ex-Mayor of Monrovia and CDC National Secretary General (letter to President Trump)
a3030.name: Jefferson T. Koijee
a3030.title: Ex-Mayor of Monrovia and CDC National Secretary General (letter to President Trump)
a3030.speech: Pleads with Trump to reconsider the planned deportation of 1,563 Liberians currently residing in the United States, noting that many fled political persecution and violence back home and have contributed immensely to the U.S. economy and Liberia's development through remittances: “Deporting them under President Boakai's regime—marked by widespread rape, murder, and economic collapse—would endanger their lives and devastate their families” ; reminds Trump of his previous policies on Liberia, including his 2018 extension of Deferred Enforced Departure (DED) and the 2019 enactment of the Liberian Refugee Immigration Fairness (LRIF) provision, pleading, “A similar act of compassion today would strengthen U.S.-Liberia relations and safeguard thousands of vulnerable individuals.”

a3030.speaker: Jefferson T. Koijee, Ex-Mayor of Monrovia and CDC National Secretary General (letter to President Trump)
a3030.name: Jefferson T. Koijee
a3030.title: Ex-Mayor of Monrovia and CDC National Secretary General (letter to President Trump)
a3030.speech: Outlines a plethora of issues including misuse of U.S. foreign aid that he says has led to deep social and political crises, citing the government's alleged cancelation of a $17 million tax advisory project and lack of proper accountability for US$1.5 million allocated by USAID for voter confidence ; recommends, “Given this level of mismanagement, Liberia is unprepared to handle direct foreign aid under President Boakai. A full-scale investigation into previous USAID grants to Liberia is necessary, particularly the $1.5 million allocated for voter confidence” ; notes that as a former Mayor of Monrovia he had previously warned the U.S. government that USAID funds were being used to manipulate electoral integrity, and that evidence has since emerged that the Election Coordinating Committee (ECC), which received these funds, was actively colluding with the ruling Unity Party: “USAID's unwavering support for the ECC, as expressed by Ms. Catherine Rodriguez, was an unacceptable intrusion into Liberia's political system.”

a3030.speaker: Jefferson T. Koijee, Ex-Mayor of Monrovia and CDC National Secretary General (letter to President Trump)
a3030.name: Jefferson T. Koijee
a3030.title: Ex-Mayor of Monrovia and CDC National Secretary General (letter to President Trump)
a3030.speech: “President Joseph Boakai has consistently violated our nation's laws, undermining democratic accountability and the very foundations on which our democracy was built.” ; accuses Boakai of orchestrating a legislative coup d'état by using state resources to remove a legally elected Speaker, Cllr. J. Fonati Koffa, in an effort to consolidate control over the Legislature and interfere with fiscal policy ; notes that the Boakai Administration is operating a treasonable budget, one that was not signed by the duly elected Speaker, thereby eliminating necessary checks and balances in governance.

a3030.speaker: Article 76, Section 5 of the Liberian Constitution (cited document)
a3030.name: Article 76
a3030.title: Section 5 of the Liberian Constitution (cited document)
a3030.speech: Defines treasonable acts as, “Abrogating or attempting to abrogate, subverting or attempting or conspiring to subvert the Constitution by use of force or show of force or any other means which attempts to undermine this Constitution.”

a3030.speaker: Jefferson T. Koijee, Ex-Mayor of Monrovia and CDC National Secretary General (letter to President Trump)
a3030.name: Jefferson T. Koijee
a3030.title: Ex-Mayor of Monrovia and CDC National Secretary General (letter to President Trump)
a3030.speech: Says human rights violations under the government have reached an unprecedented level, with over one hundred reported deaths in just one year, saying “These deaths stem from state-sponsored persecution, sodomy, gang rape, police brutality, and ritualistic killings. Despite these grave atrocities, the President has failed to reconcile our nation, exacerbating Liberia's deep wounds and hindering collective national development and peace.”

a3030.speaker: Jefferson T. Koijee, Ex-Mayor of Monrovia and CDC National Secretary General (letter to President Trump)
a3030.name: Jefferson T. Koijee
a3030.title: Ex-Mayor of Monrovia and CDC National Secretary General (letter to President Trump)
a3030.speech: Continues that the President has engaged in political harassment against institutions and individuals who express dissent, recalling that on August 5 and 22, 2024, police violently invaded the headquarters of the Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC), attacking peaceful citizens and causing over $50,000 in property damage ; notes that Boakai instructed the Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of Liberia to deploy soldiers at Roberts International Airport to prevent former President George Weah from accessing the VIP Lounge: “This act of state-sanctioned intimidation nearly resulted in an assassination attempt on former President Weah on June 6, 2024. Additionally, Liberians who welcomed Weah on this day were brutally assaulted.” ; says the President influenced the arbitrary dismissal of numerous employees at the Monrovia City Government for expressing grievances on social media, which he describes as a clear violation of their constitutional rights.

a3030.speaker: Jefferson T. Koijee, Ex-Mayor of Monrovia and CDC National Secretary General (letter to President Trump)
a3030.name: Jefferson T. Koijee
a3030.title: Ex-Mayor of Monrovia and CDC National Secretary General (letter to President Trump)
a3030.speech: Details that when President Boakai took office with his “Rescue Mission” he pledged to fight corruption and uphold good governance, but that this administration has become a hub of financial misconduct, citing US$2.3 million in unaccounted miscellaneous expenses; US$15 million in off-budget expenditures; US$100,000 transferred onto the President's personal debit card for unauthorized transactions; US$374,239.24 paid to former Central Bank Governor Aloysius Tarlue to coerce his resignation; and US$75,000 allocated for a $45,000 vehicle for the National Oil Company of Liberia's CEO, Rustonlyn Suacoco Dennis, inflating costs through fraud ; “Despite these glaring cases of corruption, millions of Liberians lack access to clean drinking water, electricity, employment, and healthcare.”

a3030.speaker: Jefferson T. Koijee, Ex-Mayor of Monrovia and CDC National Secretary General (letter to President Trump)
a3030.name: Jefferson T. Koijee
a3030.title: Ex-Mayor of Monrovia and CDC National Secretary General (letter to President Trump)
a3030.speech: Applauds the U.S. Department of Government Efficiency under billionaire Elon Musk for exposing corruption within USAID and in countries like Liberia, while stressing that investigating foreign aid misuse is a necessary step toward accountability and reform to ensure that American taxpayers' money is used appropriately.

a3030.speaker: Jefferson T. Koijee, Ex-Mayor of Monrovia and CDC National Secretary General (letter to President Trump)
a3030.name: Jefferson T. Koijee
a3030.title: Ex-Mayor of Monrovia and CDC National Secretary General (letter to President Trump)
a3030.speech: Lauds President Trump for restoring the image of the Holy Bible in the White House and across America, adding that establishment of the Faith Advisory Council is a monumental step in preserving religious freedom and combatting radical gender ideologies: “Your leadership in this area mirrors the biblical role of Cyrus, the Persian ruler who liberated the Jews from Babylon.”

a3039.speaker: Jefferson T. Koijee, National Secretary General of the Congress for Democratic Change and former Mayor of Monrovia (letter to President Trump)
a3039.name: Jefferson T. Koijee
a3039.title: National Secretary General of the Congress for Democratic Change and former Mayor of Monrovia (letter to President Trump)
a3039.speech: Expressed open support for nearly all the policy-weightlifting taking place under Trump's second term, except for the immigration policy deporting undocumented aliens also affecting Liberians: “One year ago, I envisioned that the United States of America would once again elect you as President. I was optimistic that the regional and global problems that persisted under the Democrats—corruption, democratic instability, continuous aggression in the Middle East, major human rights violations, and the growing threat of the sexual revolution—would come to an end.” ; “In particular, our world has been subjected to an unending redefinition of sexual identities and orientations, diverting American taxpayer funds from addressing real existential problems in human history to promoting gender revisionism in vulnerable African nations and even within the United States itself. In Africa, the issue extends far beyond teaching a boy to be a girl or a girl to be a boy. Our fundamental challenges stem from within, and we must stand in solidarity with a leader like you, whose vision aligns with the deep desires of both the African and American people.” ; “Your presidency comes at a critical time when nations are failing to establish mechanisms for self-reliance while simultaneously imposing artificial hardships on their citizens. I am confident that your leadership will promote self-sufficiency, personal responsibility, and the values of self-determination. We are tired of being beggars in a land endowed with God-given natural resources—resources that should be used to feed our people and eradicate extreme poverty.”

a3039.speaker: Jefferson T. Koijee, National Secretary General of the Congress for Democratic Change and former Mayor of Monrovia (letter to President Trump)
a3039.name: Jefferson T. Koijee
a3039.title: National Secretary General of the Congress for Democratic Change and former Mayor of Monrovia (letter to President Trump)
a3039.speech: “In Liberia, the misuse of U.S. foreign aid has led to deep social and political crises. For example, the $17 million tax advisory project was canceled, and USAID allocated $1.5 million for voter confidence—yet our country remains mired in corruption and instability.” ; “Given this level of mismanagement, Liberia is unprepared to handle direct foreign aid under President Boakai. A full-scale investigation into previous USAID grants to Liberia is necessary—particularly the $1.5 million allocated for voter confidence.” ; “As the former Mayor of Monrovia, I previously warned the U.S. government that USAID funds were being used to manipulate electoral integrity. Evidence has since emerged that the Election Coordinating Committee (ECC), which received these funds, was actively colluding with the ruling Unity Party. USAID's unwavering support for the ECC, as expressed by Ms. Catherine Rodriguez, was an unacceptable intrusion into Liberia's political system.”

a3039.speaker: Jefferson T. Koijee, National Secretary General of the Congress for Democratic Change and former Mayor of Monrovia (letter to President Trump)
a3039.name: Jefferson T. Koijee
a3039.title: National Secretary General of the Congress for Democratic Change and former Mayor of Monrovia (letter to President Trump)
a3039.speech: “President Joseph Boakai has consistently violated our nation's laws, undermining democratic accountability and the very foundations on which our democracy was built. He orchestrated a legislative coup d'état by using state resources to remove a legally elected Speaker, Cllr. J. Fonati Koffa, in an effort to consolidate control over the Legislature and interfere with fiscal policy. Additionally, he is operating a treasonable budget—one that was not signed by the duly elected Speaker—thereby eliminating the necessary checks and balances in governance.”

a3039.speaker: Article 76, Section 5 of the Liberian Constitution (cited document)
a3039.name: Article 76
a3039.title: Section 5 of the Liberian Constitution (cited document)
a3039.speech: “Abrogating or attempting to abrogate, subverting or attempting or conspiring to subvert the Constitution by use of force or show of force or any other means which attempts to undermine this Constitution.”

a3039.speaker: Jefferson T. Koijee, National Secretary General of the Congress for Democratic Change and former Mayor of Monrovia (letter to President Trump)
a3039.name: Jefferson T. Koijee
a3039.title: National Secretary General of the Congress for Democratic Change and former Mayor of Monrovia (letter to President Trump)
a3039.speech: “Under President Boakai, human rights violations have reached an unprecedented level, with over one hundred reported deaths in just one year. These deaths stem from state-sponsored persecution, sodomy, gang rape, police brutality, and ritualistic killings. Despite these grave atrocities, the President has failed to reconcile our nation, exacerbating Liberia's deep wounds and hindering collective national development and peace.” ; “President Boakai has also engaged in political harassment against institutions and individuals who express dissent. On August 5 and 22, 2024, police violently invaded the headquarters of the Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC), attacking peaceful citizens and causing over $50,000 in property damage. Furthermore, President Boakai instructed the Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of Liberia to deploy soldiers at the airport to prevent former President George Weah from accessing the VIP Lounge upon his arrival. This act of state-sanctioned intimidation nearly resulted in an assassination attempt on former President Weah on June 6, 2024. Additionally, Liberians who welcomed Weah on this day were brutally assaulted.” ; “The President has also influenced the arbitrary dismissal of numerous employees at the Monrovia City Government for simply expressing their grievances on social media—a clear violation of their constitutional rights.”

a3039.speaker: Jefferson T. Koijee, National Secretary General of the Congress for Democratic Change and former Mayor of Monrovia (letter to President Trump)
a3039.name: Jefferson T. Koijee
a3039.title: National Secretary General of the Congress for Democratic Change and former Mayor of Monrovia (letter to President Trump)
a3039.speech: “When President Boakai assumed office under his so-called ‘Rescue Mission,’ he pledged to fight corruption and uphold good governance. However, his administration has become a hub of financial misconduct.” Notable cases he lists include $2.3 million in unaccounted miscellaneous expenses; $15 million in off-budget expenditures; $100,000 transferred onto the President's personal debit card for unauthorized transactions; $374,239.24 paid to former Central Bank Governor Aloysius Tarlue to coerce his resignation; and $75,000 allocated for a $45,000 vehicle for the National Oil Company of Liberia's CEO, Rustonlyn Suacoco Dennis, inflating costs through fraud ; “Despite these glaring cases of corruption, millions of Liberians lack access to clean drinking water, electricity, employment, and healthcare.”

a3039.speaker: Jefferson T. Koijee, National Secretary General of the Congress for Democratic Change and former Mayor of Monrovia (letter to President Trump)
a3039.name: Jefferson T. Koijee
a3039.title: National Secretary General of the Congress for Democratic Change and former Mayor of Monrovia (letter to President Trump)
a3039.speech: “I want to extend my sincere appreciation to the U.S. Department of Government Efficiency and Elon Musk for exposing corruption within USAID and in countries like Liberia. Investigating foreign aid misuse is a necessary step toward accountability and reform, ensuring that American taxpayer money is used appropriately.”

a3039.speaker: Jefferson T. Koijee, National Secretary General of the Congress for Democratic Change and former Mayor of Monrovia (letter to President Trump)
a3039.name: Jefferson T. Koijee
a3039.title: National Secretary General of the Congress for Democratic Change and former Mayor of Monrovia (letter to President Trump)
a3039.speech: “President Trump, I urge you to reconsider the deportation of 1,563 Liberians currently residing in the United States. Many of them fled political persecution and violence and have contributed immensely to both the U.S. economy and Liberia's development through remittances. Deporting them under President Boakai's regime—marked by widespread rape, murder, and economic collapse—would endanger their lives and devastate their families.” ; “Your previous policies demonstrated a commitment to protecting Liberians, including your 2018 extension of Deferred Enforced Departure (DED) and the 2019 enactment of the Liberian Refugee Immigration Fairness (LRIF) provision. A similar act of compassion today would strengthen U.S.-Liberia relations and safeguard thousands of vulnerable individuals.”

a3039.speaker: Jefferson T. Koijee, National Secretary General of the Congress for Democratic Change and former Mayor of Monrovia (letter to President Trump)
a3039.name: Jefferson T. Koijee
a3039.title: National Secretary General of the Congress for Democratic Change and former Mayor of Monrovia (letter to President Trump)
a3039.speech: “As a devout Christian, I am grateful for your efforts to restore the image of the Holy Bible in the White House and across America. The establishment of the Faith Advisory Council is a monumental step in preserving religious freedom and combatting radical gender ideologies. Your leadership in this area mirrors the biblical role of Cyrus, the Persian ruler who liberated the Jews from Babylon.”

a3039.speaker: Jefferson T. Koijee, National Secretary General of the Congress for Democratic Change and former Mayor of Monrovia (letter to President Trump)
a3039.name: Jefferson T. Koijee
a3039.title: National Secretary General of the Congress for Democratic Change and former Mayor of Monrovia (letter to President Trump)
a3039.speech: “Mr. President, as the former Mayor of Monrovia and Secretary General of the Congress for Democratic Change, I implore you to stand with the Liberian people in our fight against corruption, human rights violations, and democratic erosion. Liberia has always shared a deep historical bond with the United States. Our capital city, Monrovia, is named after President James Monroe, and our largest hospital honors President John F. Kennedy. Today, we look to you as a leader who can help guide Liberia through its current crisis. Your leadership is critical in protecting Liberians at home and abroad, ensuring accountability in U.S. foreign aid, and defending the values that define both of our nations.”

a3208.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a3208.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a3208.speech: Said the recent suspension of aid to African countries provides an opportunity for affected countries to get rid of aid dependency and embrace a new era of sovereignty ; equally agrees in self-reliance and partnerships within African countries.

a3208.speaker: Tedros Gebreyesus, WHO Director General
a3208.name: Tedros Gebreyesus
a3208.title: WHO Director General
a3208.speech: Revealed during a session of the WHO regional committee for Africa, currently taking place in Lusaka, Zambia, that the organisation is scaling down over 600 jobs to redirect resources to address a 40% deficit in the global health sector.

a3208.speaker: African Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a3208.name: African Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a3208.speech: Has called for local investment in the health sector.

a3208.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, President of Zambia
a3208.name: Hakainde Hichilema
a3208.title: President of Zambia
a3208.speech: Has called for preparedness for pandemics, adding that countries need to build resilience to respond to pandemics.

a3232.speaker: Nigeria-US Parliamentary Friendship Group of the House of Representatives
a3232.name: Nigeria-US Parliamentary Friendship Group of the House of Representatives
a3232.speech: Has voiced concerns over potential US plans to designate Nigeria as a "Country of Particular Concern" (CPC) due to ongoing insecurity and violence; the group reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening diplomatic and legislative ties with the US, aiming to enhance Nigeria's role in international peace and security decisions; during their US visit, the Nigerian delegation reported meeting with the UN Deputy Secretary-General, where they emphasized the need to leverage existing UN agencies for mutual benefit.

a3232.speaker: Hon. Jesse Okey-Joe Onuakalusi, Chairman of the Nigeria-US Parliamentary Friendship Group
a3232.name: Hon. Jesse Okey-Joe Onuakalusi
a3232.title: Chairman of the Nigeria-US Parliamentary Friendship Group
a3232.speech: Emphasized that the security challenges facing Nigeria stem from criminal activities and the proliferation of arms after the Arab Spring rather than religious persecution; "Placing Nigeria on the CPC list could hinder us from accessing technology to combat crime effectively," he warned at the Nigerian House in New York.

a3232.speaker: Hon. Jesse Okey-Joe Onuakalusi, Chairman of the Nigeria-US Parliamentary Friendship Group
a3232.name: Hon. Jesse Okey-Joe Onuakalusi
a3232.title: Chairman of the Nigeria-US Parliamentary Friendship Group
a3232.speech: Pushed for Nigeria's longstanding bid for a permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council, highlighting the country's contributions to peacekeeping missions and its significant youth population as assets for global partnership and investment; further underscored Nigeria's shift from seeking foreign aid to promoting business collaborations, citing the nation's demographic and economic potential: "We are no longer interested in aids but business investments."

a3232.speaker: Hon. Dabo Ismail Haruna, member representing Toro Federal Constituency and Chairman of the Subcommittee on Protection of Critical National Assets
a3232.name: Hon. Dabo Ismail Haruna
a3232.title: member representing Toro Federal Constituency and Chairman of the Subcommittee on Protection of Critical National Assets
a3232.speech: Echoed concerns about the potential consequences of Nigeria being designated a CPC by the US; highlighted that negative reports from some Nigerians abroad are influencing US congressional deliberations, which could result in sanctions; said they have appealed directly to US lawmakers, including the Minority Leader and key committee chairs, urging that Nigeria not be added to the CPC list; called for deeper parliamentary engagement: "We will provide genuine information to strengthen our relationship with them."

a3232.speaker: Ambassador Syndoph Endoni, Nigeria's Permanent Mission to the UN
a3232.name: Ambassador Syndoph Endoni
a3232.title: Nigeria's Permanent Mission to the UN
a3232.speech: Recounted a recent meeting where he challenged the assertion that Africa lacks peace-making mechanisms, noting the roles of the African Union (AU) and ECOWAS in regional stability; stressed the importance of Nigeria having a permanent representative at the UN to effectively project the country's interests and mediate on its behalf.

a3232.speaker: Nigerian delegates to the US
a3232.name: Nigerian delegates to the US
a3232.speech: The delegates also raised concerns over Nigeria's lack of representation as chair of the UN's C34 peacekeeping committee for the past two years, noting that this absence undermines Nigeria's bid for a permanent Security Council seat; they argued that active participation and leadership in such international bodies are essential for Nigeria to be seen as a serious and credible nation for a permanent seat in the Security Council.

a3617.speaker: Maïmouna Mbacke, country director of TechnoServe-Benin
a3617.name: Maïmouna Mbacke
a3617.title: country director of TechnoServe-Benin
a3617.speech: Indicated that the ecosystem approach was chosen in order to reach more beneficiaries through the principle of delegated implementation (“faire-faire”), and explained that the aim is not only to consolidate the impact of phase 1 of the project (2017-2022) through scaling up and local anchoring, but also to reach more partners in order to ensure the sustainability of the gains.

a3617.speaker: Mathias Y. Affomaï, technical adviser for monitoring reforms and projects at Benin’s Ministry of Secondary Education and Technical and Vocational Training, member of the project steering committee
a3617.name: Mathias Y. Affomaï
a3617.title: technical adviser for monitoring reforms and projects at Benin’s Ministry of Secondary Education and Technical and Vocational Training, member of the project steering committee
a3617.speech: Said the initiative comes at just the right moment to take support for Benin’s young entrepreneurs further through training and personalised coaching; opening the proceedings, he reiterated the commitment of public and private actors to carry out their respective missions through to completion and urged participants to put into practice the lessons received.

a3617.speaker: Sigrid Meijer, First Secretary for Food and Nutrition Security at the Embassy of the Netherlands in Benin
a3617.name: Sigrid Meijer
a3617.title: First Secretary for Food and Nutrition Security at the Embassy of the Netherlands in Benin
a3617.speech: Hopes that the introduction of the MSD approach will enable the project to achieve the expected results through a combination of activities applied to the main components — skills, access to finance, access to markets and access to information; reported that the system has proved itself successfully in other countries and even in Benin, adding that the ultimate aim is to create wealth and jobs for young people and women; and, on behalf of the technical and financial partners, gave assurances of the readiness of the Dutch and Swiss cooperation agencies and of the European Union delegation to support the project.

a3617.speaker: Sigrid Meijer, First Secretary for Food and Nutrition Security at the Embassy of the Netherlands in Benin
a3617.name: Sigrid Meijer
a3617.title: First Secretary for Food and Nutrition Security at the Embassy of the Netherlands in Benin
a3617.speech: Supported the point that the inclusive markets (IM) or MSD approach has been implemented for twenty years as a way of “doing development differently”, applied successfully in a range of contexts and market systems — robust, fluctuating (as in northern Ghana) or conflict-affected (as in Chad) — and noted that other donors and development organisations use the methodology, notably the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC), the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), and the British government’s Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (UK Aid Direct).

a3617.speaker: Clara Garcia Parra, consultant with the firm Canopy Lab and lead trainer
a3617.name: Clara Garcia Parra
a3617.title: consultant with the firm Canopy Lab and lead trainer
a3617.speech: Underlined that the systemic approach refers to a set of elements coordinated by a law or theory and considered in their relationships within a whole functioning in a unitary manner; said Market Systems Development was born out of the need not to distort business support structures and that it offers tools for grasping the complexity and dynamics of project implementation contexts and for progressively remedying underlying constraints; and added that this indirect approach encourages inclusive behaviour by market system actors through mixed tactics and constant iteration during implementation, relying on an interactive process of monitoring and evaluation that allows adaptive management.

a3658.speaker: Central Bank of Lesotho (CBL) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)
a3658.name: Central Bank of Lesotho (CBL) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)
a3658.speech: Reduced the repo rate by 25 basis points, from 7.25 percent to 7 percent, a decision aimed at aligning monetary policy with current domestic economic conditions and the broader regional monetary environment ; also resolved to reduce the Net International Reserves (NIR) target floor from USD840 million to USD830 million.

a3658.speaker: Maluke Letete, Governor of the Central Bank of Lesotho
a3658.name: Maluke Letete
a3658.title: Governor of the Central Bank of Lesotho
a3658.speech: Announced the decision following the MPC's 113th meeting this week ; explained that the adjustment to the NIR target floor helps ensure the sustainability of the one-to-one peg between the Loti and the South African rand.

a3658.speaker: Maluke Letete, Governor of the Central Bank of Lesotho
a3658.name: Maluke Letete
a3658.title: Governor of the Central Bank of Lesotho
a3658.speech: Said global economic performance was mixed in the first quarter of 2025: "While major economies grew, momentum was uneven. The United States and the United Kingdom lost steam due to weaker consumer and government spending, respectively," ; "In contrast, the Euro area remained stable, supported by domestic demand, while Japan benefited from strong exports." ; "This dimmer outlook reflects mounting trade barriers, particularly tariffs, which are beginning to choke investment flows and erode business confidence. The risks are many: shaky financial markets, uncertain policy direction, slowing productivity, and escalating geopolitical stress," ; "In South Africa, inflation edged up modestly due to rising food and transport costs. In response, most central banks have cut interest rates to stimulate growth while maintaining a cautious stance amid persistent inflationary pressures and ongoing global trade tensions, particularly those linked to US tariffs."

a3658.speaker: Maluke Letete, Governor of the Central Bank of Lesotho
a3658.name: Maluke Letete
a3658.title: Governor of the Central Bank of Lesotho
a3658.speech: Said Lesotho's economy contracted by 5.3 percent in the first quarter of 2025, attributed to weak household consumption, reduced government spending, and sluggish performance in the transport and construction sectors: "While the manufacturing and financial services sectors showed some resilience, bolstered by textile exports and credit growth, overall momentum remains fragile. The outlook is clouded by rising tariffs affecting textiles, the withdrawal of key development support such as the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC), and continued weakness in the diamond market." ; said global growth is expected to remain fragile amid persistent trade barriers and heightened uncertainty, and that domestic growth remains subdued, reflecting the adverse effects of tariffs on Lesotho's exports.

a3658.speaker: Maluke Letete, Governor of the Central Bank of Lesotho
a3658.name: Maluke Letete
a3658.title: Governor of the Central Bank of Lesotho
a3658.speech: Explained that inflation relief in April 2025 (4.0 percent, down from 4.2 percent in March) came as global oil prices softened and the loti appreciated against the US dollar, resulting in lower fuel costs, and said inflation was expected to remain contained, although risks remain: "Rising global trade tensions and policy uncertainty could still exert upward pressure on prices."

a3658.speaker: Maluke Letete, Governor of the Central Bank of Lesotho
a3658.name: Maluke Letete
a3658.title: Governor of the Central Bank of Lesotho
a3658.speech: Said Lesotho maintained a disciplined and supportive fiscal stance in the first quarter of 2025, achieving a 12.9 percent budget surplus despite weaker VAT collections linked to compliance challenges ; said the current account surplus narrowed to 0.7 percent of GDP in Q1 2025, reflecting weaker exports and rising service outflows, with reserves healthy at 5.3 months of import cover ; "The CBL's Net International Reserves increased by approximately USD 40.30 million - from USD 1,028.90 million on 13 March 2025 to USD 1,069.21 million on 21 May 2025 - mainly driven by SACU receipts. The NIR position is projected to improve further in the near to medium term."

a3658.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a3658.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a3658.speech: Global growth is now forecast at 2.8 percent in 2025, a downgrade driven by rising trade tensions and protectionist measures that are weighing on investment and business confidence.

a3837.speaker: USAID/State Accountability, Transparency and Effectiveness (State2State) Activity
a3837.name: USAID/State Accountability
a3837.title: Transparency and Effectiveness (State2State) Activity
a3837.speech: Has called for improved budgetary implementation and performance in the health, education, and water, sanitation and hygiene sectors in Adamawa State.

a3837.speaker: Suzanne Myada, Adamawa Team Lead, USAID State2State
a3837.name: Suzanne Myada
a3837.title: Adamawa Team Lead, USAID State2State
a3837.speech: Explained that since 2020 State2State has been complementing the efforts of the State and Local Government Areas by supporting and sustaining the ongoing public financial management and other reforms as well as providing training, building skills and capacity of the stakeholders in the State ; Underscored the need to invest in the people through the provision of health care systems, education, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene sectors, adding that the people remain the greatest resource in the State ; As the State2State Activity ends in 2025 in the State, called on the members of the Adamawa State House of Assembly and key stakeholders to take ownership of the programme, align the State's plans with local government areas, harmonise their activities to forestall duplication as well as focus on development results for mutual accountability.

a3837.speaker: Stanley Achonu, Deputy Chief of Party, USAID State2State
a3837.name: Stanley Achonu
a3837.title: Deputy Chief of Party, USAID State2State
a3837.speech: Urged the members of the Adamawa State House of Assembly to ensure the sustainability of the Activity, after the programme has ended in 2025 ; Tasked the members of the Assembly to organise quarterly budget performance hearing with heads of Ministries, Departments and Agencies as part of their oversight function geared towards scrutinising the implementation of the state budget for optimal performance ; Assured that State2State would continue to provide technical support to the members of the Assembly, for the overall welfare of the people of Adamawa State.

a3837.speaker: Rt. Hon. Bathiya Wesley, Speaker of Adamawa State House of Assembly
a3837.name: Rt. Hon. Bathiya Wesley
a3837.title: Speaker of Adamawa State House of Assembly
a3837.speech: In his opening remarks, commended USAID/State2State for organising the two-day event ; Said effective implementation of budget in the State would improve the standard of living for Adamawa people ; Assured that the members of the Adamawa State House of Assembly would continue to provide oversight function on the implementation of the approved budget in the State.

a3837.speaker: Allahdon Kenan, State2State Public Financial Management Specialist
a3837.name: Allahdon Kenan
a3837.title: State2State Public Financial Management Specialist
a3837.speech: In his presentation, took a holistic view on the performance of the Adamawa State budget from 2019 to 2024: budget performance in the state in 2019 was 38.33%; 2020 (43.03%); 2021 (71.33%); 2022 (66.23%); 2023 (74.95%) while in 2024 (January-September) it stood at 68.56% ; While observing a decline in the budgetary allocations to health, education and WASH sectors, appealed to the members of the Adamawa State House of Assembly to scale up the budget in these sectors for the overall benefits of the people in the State.

a3869.speaker: Kimberly Rosen, Mission Director for USAID/Ghana
a3869.name: Kimberly Rosen
a3869.title: Mission Director for USAID/Ghana
a3869.speech: Emphasised the strategic importance of the motorcycles in assisting the tireless community healthcare officers and volunteers who face challenging conditions such as bad roads, flooding and long days away from home; she also recognised the crucial role of district health directors and the Health Administration and Support Services Division (HASS) in ensuring the maintenance and readiness of the motorbikes for service, indicating that "investing in primary health care is the most efficient way to ensure good health."

a3869.speaker: Dr Ebo Hammond, Director of Health Administration and Support Services (HASS), Ghana Health Service
a3869.name: Dr Ebo Hammond
a3869.title: Director of Health Administration and Support Services (HASS), Ghana Health Service
a3869.speech: Expressed appreciation to USAID and indicated that the motorbikes were more than just mobility equipment. “They are essential tools for healthcare delivery,” he said ; explained that in some rural areas, four-wheel vehicles could not access the communities, making motorbikes an invaluable asset ; "A motorbike with a bussing carrier behind, with a nurse on it can save lives."

a3869.speaker: Dr Ebo Hammond, Director of Health Administration and Support Services (HASS), Ghana Health Service
a3869.name: Dr Ebo Hammond
a3869.title: Director of Health Administration and Support Services (HASS), Ghana Health Service
a3869.speech: Reflected on USAID's broader impact, particularly in leveraging medical-grade oxygen around the country: "Because of these investments, it reduced the distance to access from 1,850 to 850 kilometres. And the good news is that currently, through USAID’s support, we are also installing 10 liquid oxygen plants all around the country."

a3869.speaker: Dr Peter Yeboah, Executive Director of the Christian Health Association of Ghana (CHAG)
a3869.name: Dr Peter Yeboah
a3869.title: Executive Director of the Christian Health Association of Ghana (CHAG)
a3869.speech: Said the motorbikes were vital investments and affirmed CHAG's commitment to using the equipment for their intended purpose: "We will use these motorbikes for their intended use, ensure that we capacitate health workforce at that level who will be able to reach remote communities otherwise unreached."

a3919.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a3919.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a3919.speech: Warned on Tuesday that several areas in the south of the Sudanese capital Khartoum are threatened with famine, denouncing a critical funding shortfall that hampers humanitarian aid in a country ravaged by two years of conflict ; announced that it had reached one million people in seven localities of Khartoum after regaining access to the capital ; says it is currently assisting 4 million people a month in Sudan, four times more than at the beginning of 2024, with the objective of reaching 7 million monthly beneficiaries, prioritising areas threatened by famine such as Darfur, Kordofan, Al Jazira and Khartoum ; sounds the alarm in the face of a 500-million-dollar shortfall for the next six months.

a3919.speaker: Laurent Bukera, WFP Representative in Sudan
a3919.name: Laurent Bukera
a3919.title: WFP Representative in Sudan
a3919.speech: « The level of hunger, destitution and despair observed is severe and confirms the risk of famine in these regions. » ; painted a bleak picture of the situation in the capital: « We have witnessed massive destruction, limited access to water, health care and electricity, as well as a cholera epidemic. In some parts of the city life is resuming, but many neighbourhoods remain abandoned, like a ghost town. »

a3919.speaker: Laurent Bukera, WFP Representative in Sudan
a3919.name: Laurent Bukera
a3919.title: WFP Representative in Sudan
a3919.speech: Deplored, after a WFP and UNICEF convoy was attacked near El Koma in the Darfur region last week, killing five and wounding many: « Indiscriminate and unacceptable attacks on humanitarian personnel and operations are multiplying. »

a3919.speaker: Laurent Bukera, WFP Representative in Sudan
a3919.name: Laurent Bukera
a3919.title: WFP Representative in Sudan
a3919.speech: Insisted: « The international community must act now, by increasing funding to stop famine in the worst-affected areas », warning that further cuts in aid will be inevitable without additional funding.

a4193.speaker: Jacqueline “Jacky” Goliath, managing director of De Fynne wholesale nursery
a4193.name: Jacqueline “Jacky” Goliath
a4193.title: managing director of De Fynne wholesale nursery
a4193.speech: today she “wouldn't change anything” ; attributes their success to their complementing personalities — she's more practical and hands-on, running the farm, whereas Elton is more strategic and business-oriented. “It's usually a very male-dominated industry. It was even more challenging as a previously disadvantaged black man and woman with no money or land,” Jacky adds.

a4193.speaker: Jacqueline “Jacky” Goliath, managing director of De Fynne wholesale nursery
a4193.name: Jacqueline “Jacky” Goliath
a4193.title: managing director of De Fynne wholesale nursery
a4193.speech: she shares the accolades with the 28-strong staff members, “I like to bring the awards back to the people. You need to build relationships.”

a4473.speaker: Arab League (statement)
a4473.name: Arab League (statement)
a4473.speech: Announced that the Syrian government had accepted a proposal by the League to halt violence in Syria, and said in a statement following a meeting in Cairo, “The Arab League welcomes the Syrian government's agreement to the Arab plan”, adding that it “emphasised the need for the immediate, full and exact implementation of the articles in the plan”.

a4473.speaker: Syrian state news report
a4473.name: Syrian state news report
a4473.speech: Claimed on Monday that Syrian authorities had agreed to terms with an Arab League ministerial committee on a plan to end the violence.

a4473.speaker: United Nations
a4473.name: United Nations
a4473.speech: Says the number of people killed in the seven-month-old uprising has surpassed 3,000.

a4473.speaker: Syrian government
a4473.name: Syrian government
a4473.speech: Throughout the uprising has defended its actions with the claim that terrorists had killed hundreds of security personnel.

a4473.speaker: Bashar Al-Assad, Syrian President
a4473.name: Bashar Al-Assad
a4473.title: Syrian President
a4473.speech: Admitted to Britain’s Sunday Telegraph that his security forces had indeed made “some mistakes”.

a4473.speaker: Syrian activists
a4473.name: Syrian activists
a4473.speech: Claimed at least 34 people were killed in the restive provinces of Homs and Hama ahead of the Arab League’s announcement on Wednesday.

a4473.speaker: Syrian Revolution General Commission (SRGC)
a4473.name: Syrian Revolution General Commission (SRGC)
a4473.speech: Said it rejected the Arab League plan; for them only a toppling of the regime would be acceptable.

a4473.speaker: Representatives of the Arab League
a4473.name: Representatives of the Arab League
a4473.speech: Indicated to the media that if the plan was not implemented, the Arab foreign ministers would reconvene to “reconsider further steps”.

a4527.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a4527.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a4527.title: President of South Africa
a4527.speech: At the announcement of Mcebisi Jonas's appointment, recalled the importance of the “historic and strategic” ties between the two countries and insisted on his desire to restore bilateral cooperation based on respect for sovereignty and mutual interests; stressed that trade between the two nations “must remain free, predictable and governed by a rules-based system”.

a4527.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a4527.name: Donald Trump
a4527.title: President of the United States
a4527.speech: Made accusations against South Africa, notably on the sensitive question of the expropriation of farmland, which the American president interpreted as an attack on the country’s white minority; also voiced virulent criticism of South African foreign policy, notably its action against Israel at the International Court of Justice.

a4527.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a4527.name: Donald Trump
a4527.title: President of the United States
a4527.speech: Threatened to boycott the G20 summit planned for Johannesburg, calling into question South African leadership on the international stage.

a4691.speaker: ActionAid study, ‘The human cost of public sector cuts in Africa’ (report)
a4691.name: ActionAid study
a4691.title: ‘The human cost of public sector cuts in Africa’ (report)
a4691.speech: Faulted International Monetary Fund (IMF) policies in poor countries, saying they have led to deterioration of public services ; highlights that developing countries tend to prioritise repayment of foreign debt at the expense of social spending in sectors such as health, education and agriculture ; found that in 2024, external debt payments as percentage of national revenue was 25.4 percent while spending on health stood at 5.74 percent and public sector wage bill as percent of gross domestic product (GDP) was 4.5 percent, but IMF still called for cuts ; shows that in 2024 alone, Malawi lost $51.3 million (about K89 billion) to illicit financial flows.

a4691.speaker: ActionAid study, ‘The human cost of public sector cuts in Africa’ (report) — on health
a4691.name: ActionAid study
a4691.title: ‘The human cost of public sector cuts in Africa’ (report) — on health
a4691.speech: Said a decline in real wages due to inflation has had negative impact on the living conditions of healthcare workers and their families, with some reporting reduced food intake and struggling with covering school-related expenses ; said that vulnerable communities were thrown into financial despair as mounting medical expenses forced families to delay or avoid treatment, only seeking medical help when conditions became critical ; “Those who do seek treatment often face financial strain, resorting to borrowing money, reducing food intake, or selling essential household items to cover medical expenses. To pay for treatment, community members, particularly in Malawi, have reported selling household assets, taking out loans, or reducing spending on essentials like food.”

a4691.speaker: ActionAid study, ‘The human cost of public sector cuts in Africa’ (report) — on education
a4691.name: ActionAid study
a4691.title: ‘The human cost of public sector cuts in Africa’ (report) — on education
a4691.speech: Reports a 40 percent budget cut to education in the last three to five years while enrollment surged due to growing demand for education, resulting in overcrowded classrooms in public schools ; said 90 percent of surveyed teachers reported that a decline in wages due to inflation left them struggling to pay their bills while 65 percent reported a decline in working conditions due to overcrowded conditions ; “This situation has negatively impacted the quality of public education services, with communities reporting significant declines in service quality since 2020, as the shortage of teachers and ballooning class sizes weakens the quality of learning.”

a4691.speaker: Solomon Chomba, Human Resources for Health chairperson
a4691.name: Solomon Chomba
a4691.title: Human Resources for Health chairperson
a4691.speech: Feared that the health sector will collapse should donors stop supporting Malawi due to the lapsing of IMF’s Extended Credit Facility (ECF) ; said the Donald Trump executive orders on aid cuts have already cost some healthcare workers jobs while other essential services and medicines were cut off ; “Let us make sure that Malawians contribute towards their health needs. Free healthcare services are not helping. Again introduce a health levy on fuel and motorists because accidents on the roads are costing us more.”

a4691.speaker: Gowokani Chijere-Chirwa, health economist
a4691.name: Gowokani Chijere-Chirwa
a4691.title: health economist
a4691.speech: Suggested compulsory health surcharge for people coming into the country.

a4691.speaker: Benedicto Kondowe, Civil Society Education Coalition executive director
a4691.name: Benedicto Kondowe
a4691.title: Civil Society Education Coalition executive director
a4691.speech: Said the situation will weaken human capital development, entrench poverty and stall socio-economic development, making it harder for the country to meet its development goals ; “There is need to increase domestic resource mobilisation, prioritising pro-poor spending, and advocating for fairer international financing terms that do not undermine essential public services.”

a4691.speaker: Limbani Nsapato, Link for Education Governance executive director
a4691.name: Limbani Nsapato
a4691.title: Link for Education Governance executive director
a4691.speech: Urged government to adopt innovative funding mechanisms including putting in place education levies, promoting diaspora investments and enhancing public private partnerships to get more resources for the budget.

a4691.speaker: Yandura Chipeta, ActionAid Malawi executive director
a4691.name: Yandura Chipeta
a4691.title: ActionAid Malawi executive director
a4691.speech: Said in the long run the inequality gap between the rich and the poor in the country will widen as free public services are bound to collapse if the situation is not reversed ; “The IMF must abandon its coercive policy. There is also need to increase grants such as the Loss and Damage Fund to developing countries like Malawi to revive its education and healthcare systems.”

a4691.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4691.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4691.speech: There was no immediate comment from the IMF yesterday.

a4691.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a4691.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a4691.title: President of Malawi
a4691.speech: Recently claimed that ‘rigid’ conditionalities under the collapsed ECF deal limited the country’s ability to spend on essential services.

a4956.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a4956.name: Daniel Chapo
a4956.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a4956.speech: Said that the theft of medicines, cross-border smuggling and the proliferation of counterfeit drugs are a real threat to public health, to the integrity of the health system and to the population's trust, and stressed that Africa's dependence on medicines produced on other continents leaves health systems vulnerable: "The theft of medicines, cross-border smuggling and the proliferation of counterfeit medicines are a real threat to public health, to the integrity of our health systems and to the population's trust." ; "these phenomena aggravate the shortage of pharmaceutical products, fuel parallel markets, undermine governance efforts and, worse still, bring disastrous consequences for public health, such as increased mortality rates from treatable diseases and the spread of antimicrobial resistance. They also bring an enormous burden for the economies of our African countries."

a4956.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a4956.name: Daniel Chapo
a4956.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a4956.speech: Explained, speaking at the opening of the "International Conference on Local Production, Research and Development of Medicines and Health Products", that it is in Africa that "the burden of disease remains heaviest, with around 25% of the global burden"; said that like many African countries "Mozambique faces high rates of infectious diseases", listing malaria, HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, cholera and the "alarming growth of chronic non-communicable diseases"; said "Around 90% of all medicines and health products that Africa consumes are produced on other continents" and that this extreme dependence places health systems in a vulnerable position, exposed to international market fluctuations, logistical delays, geopolitical crises and budgetary constraints.

a4956.speaker: World Health Organization reports (cited by President Chapo)
a4956.name: World Health Organization reports (cited by President Chapo)
a4956.speech: "the reports of the World Health Organization reported that 42% of incidents with counterfeit and falsified medicines in the years 2013 to 2017 occurred in Africa."

a4956.speaker: United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime
a4956.name: United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime
a4956.speech: Estimates that close to 500,000 deaths per year in sub-Saharan Africa are caused by the use of falsified medicines, that is, by failure of therapeutic treatment; of the total of these deaths, around 267,000 were caused by falsified antimalarials and 169,000 by falsified antibiotics.

a4956.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a4956.name: Daniel Chapo
a4956.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a4956.speech: Recalled the difficulties exposed by the COVID-19 pandemic in the global supply of medical products, as well as the urgency of strengthening local pharmaceutical production capacities; said Mozambique faced the pandemic's challenges with resilience but drew from it a very clear lesson: "no country should remain vulnerable to shortages of essential medicines, vaccines or medical equipment"; highlighted "the insufficient availability of medicines, with particular incidence in rural and hard-to-reach areas, the budgetary limitations that hinder procurement at adequate scale and quality, and the incipient pharmaceutical industrial sector" and "the structural logistical deficiencies, from storage through to distribution", saying this significantly compromises continuity of treatment.

a4956.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a4956.name: Daniel Chapo
a4956.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a4956.speech: Announced that, as of Wednesday, the country begins the official implementation of the "National Traceability System for Medicines and Health Products": medicines carry a tracking seal from manufacture to the patient, "even a medicine that is opened outside the country, smuggled, the system will flag it in Mozambique and will indicate" where the drug is located.

a4960.speaker: Gen Michael Langley, head of US Africa Command (Africom)
a4960.name: Gen Michael Langley
a4960.title: head of US Africa Command (Africom)
a4960.speech: Described the Sahel a few days ago as "The epicentre of terrorism on the globe" ; "One of the terrorists' new objectives is gaining access to West African coasts. If they secure access to the coastline, they can finance their operations through smuggling, human trafficking and arms trading. This not only puts African nations at risk but also raises the chance of threats reaching US shores." ; admitted that the current upsurge in militant attacks is "deeply concerning."

a4960.speaker: Gen Michael Langley, head of US Africa Command (Africom)
a4960.name: Gen Michael Langley
a4960.title: head of US Africa Command (Africom)
a4960.speech: Has repeatedly hammered home a core message: the US is minded to rein back its own sub-Saharan military operations, leaving local armies to take on more of the defence burden ; says there have been 25 strikes in Somalia this year, double the 2024 total ; "Some things that we used to do, we may not do anymore," he recently told a conference in Nairobi that brought together chiefs of defence staff and other senior officers from 37 countries ; "Our aim is not to serve as a permanent crutch, but to achieve US security objectives that overlap with our partners. We should be able to help African nations build the self-reliance they need to independently confront terrorism and insurgencies." ; "We have set our priorities now - protecting the homeland" - what matters to the Trump II administration, the general made clear in a Pentagon publication last week, is fighting terrorists, particularly those who might attack the US, along with countering the spread of Chinese military influence across Africa and protecting freedom of maritime navigation through key trade choke points.

a4960.speaker: Gen Michael Langley, head of US Africa Command (Africom)
a4960.name: Gen Michael Langley
a4960.title: head of US Africa Command (Africom)
a4960.speech: Lauds the National Guard State Partnership Program, through which individual US states have been helping to build the capacity of government security forces across Africa and other parts of the world for the past three decades.

a4960.speaker: Gen Michael Langley, head of US Africa Command (Africom)
a4960.name: Gen Michael Langley
a4960.title: head of US Africa Command (Africom)
a4960.speech: Only last year, in an interview with the Associated Press news agency, he outlined what he described as a "whole of government" response to the proliferation of conflict, stressing the importance of good governance and action to tackle the fragilities of African states and the impacts of desertification, crop failure and environmental change ; recently noted how Ivory Coast had countered the jihadist threat to its northern border areas by complementing security force deployments with development projects.

a4960.speaker: Gen Michael Langley, head of US Africa Command (Africom)
a4960.name: Gen Michael Langley
a4960.title: head of US Africa Command (Africom)
a4960.speech: Suggests African governments should tell Washington what they thought of the idea that Africom could be downgraded to become a subsidiary of the US command in Europe.

a4960.speaker: Gen Michael Langley, head of US Africa Command (Africom)
a4960.name: Gen Michael Langley
a4960.title: head of US Africa Command (Africom)
a4960.speech: Addressing Congress this week, warned about China's and Russia's African ambitions: Beijing's agility at capitalising on the US's absence and Moscow's ability to seize military opportunities created by chaos and instability.

a4960.speaker: US Africa Command (Africom) 2019 published list
a4960.name: US Africa Command (Africom) 2019 published list
a4960.speech: Mentioned 13 "enduring" American bases across the continent and a further 17 more temporary facilities.

a5001.speaker: Matt Bryden, founder of Sahan, a Nairobi-based think tank
a5001.name: Matt Bryden
a5001.title: founder of Sahan, a Nairobi-based think tank
a5001.speech: "The Trump administration is apparently not convinced that al-Shabab represents a direct threat to U.S. interests," and said further gains by the group "would have far-reaching implications for U.S. policy in Africa and much of the Middle East."

a5001.speaker: Former senior State Department official (anonymous)
a5001.name: Former senior State Department official (anonymous)
a5001.speech: "I sat down with people from the White House, and they asked: 'What if we just let [Somalia] burn? Can we contain it?' I said, 'No!'"

a5001.speaker: Former senior State Department official (anonymous)
a5001.name: Former senior State Department official (anonymous)
a5001.speech: Said U.S. disengagement could fuel al-Shabab's expansion into neighboring Kenya and Ethiopia and allow the Somali fighters to strengthen fledgling relations with Yemen's Houthi rebels; said the last of two recent al-Shabab-Houthi meetings involved the Houthis sending an explosives expert to Jilib, al-Shabab's de facto capital, citing U.S. intelligence.

a5001.speaker: White House official (anonymous)
a5001.name: White House official (anonymous)
a5001.speech: Acknowledged growing frustration with the Somali government, telling the Washington Post: "We are concerned about President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's prioritization of internal politics over counterterrorism efforts, particularly in light of the growing threat from al-Shabab." ; Said American officials have "repeatedly urged" Mohamud "to refocus on security cooperation and regional inclusion, and are disappointed by the lack of progress," adding that his emphasis on centralizing power "is hindering progress on counterterrorism" and "we believe a shift in priorities is essential to address the escalating threat."

a5001.speaker: State Department press office
a5001.name: State Department press office
a5001.speech: Said the United States "will continue to work closely with Somali and African Union forces."

a5001.speaker: Turkish officials
a5001.name: Turkish officials
a5001.speech: Did not respond to requests for comment.

a5001.speaker: U.N. sanctions experts
a5001.name: U.N. sanctions experts
a5001.speech: Documented two recent meetings between al-Shabab and the Houthis.

a5001.speaker: Larry Andre, former U.S. ambassador
a5001.name: Larry Andre
a5001.title: former U.S. ambassador
a5001.speech: "Things always start off great with a new president, and then clan politics makes it all fall apart," recalling coordinating outfits with the beleaguered prime minister in 2022 during a joint news conference; their matching sky-blue running suits signaled they were united, Andre said, after political rivalries sparked deadly clan battles.

a5001.speaker: Larry Andre, former U.S. ambassador
a5001.name: Larry Andre
a5001.title: former U.S. ambassador
a5001.speech: "Somalia is resource rich, but insecurity has prevented the commercialization of those resources. If we desert our partners, then others will replace us and reap the rewards when Somalia establishes peace and prosperity."

a5001.speaker: Hussein Sheikh Ali, Somalia's national security adviser
a5001.name: Hussein Sheikh Ali
a5001.title: Somalia's national security adviser
a5001.speech: Said the U.S. helps organize Somalia's seven core security partners, which include Britain, Turkey, the United Arab Emirates and the African Union; all are against al-Shabab, Ali said, but sometimes have competing agendas: "On areas of counterterrorism [the Americans] are our lead partner."

a5001.speaker: Aldebaran, a risk consultancy company
a5001.name: Aldebaran
a5001.title: a risk consultancy company
a5001.speech: According to Aldebaran, since February insurgents have taken back dozens of villages, including the strategic town of Adan Yabaal, and regained the ability to operate in nearly a third of the territory they lost to federal forces in 2022.

a5001.speaker: U.S. government audit
a5001.name: U.S. government audit
a5001.speech: A U.S. government audit last year found that Danab had padded food and fuel requisitions.

a5001.speaker: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State
a5001.name: Marco Rubio
a5001.title: U.S. Secretary of State
a5001.speech: Has said the wider freeze on foreign assistance programs under Trump will reduce government bloat and allow the administration to focus on domestic priorities.

a5001.speaker: Some former U.S. officials
a5001.name: Some former U.S. officials
a5001.speech: Say the torrent of international security funds into Somalia only fuels the country's deep-rooted corruption; others contend that continued funding to a small, select unit working alongside U.S. soldiers is the best among bad options.

a5001.speaker: Former senior U.S. military official (anonymous)
a5001.name: Former senior U.S. military official (anonymous)
a5001.speech: "If we don't directly sustain the Danab, the Somali National Army is highly unlikely to sustain them to the degree required for them to be most effective."

a5001.speaker: Former senior U.S. military official (anonymous)
a5001.name: Former senior U.S. military official (anonymous)
a5001.speech: Said that although the fight in Somalia is a grinding and protracted one, AFRICOM has seen the spending and the risk to U.S. forces as an acceptable cost to contain a potential threat; he noted that U.S. access to the Horn of Africa has decreased steadily over the past decade: "The accountant's argument might be we hand [Somalia] off to the Turks and let them handle that security problem, but the cost of reentry is significant, and we lose influence over key geographic terrain." ; "When you sacrifice that and burden-shift it to an ally … it's unlikely your interests and objectives will align."

a5001.speaker: Mogadishu-based security expert who works with the Somali military (anonymous)
a5001.name: Mogadishu-based security expert who works with the Somali military (anonymous)
a5001.speech: Said morale within Danab is "not that high"; when the stipends were cut, about 100 soldiers "went AWOL for a bit," he said, and most of Danab's foreign mentors also went home after the U.S. cuts.

a5001.speaker: U.S. security officials (anonymous)
a5001.name: U.S. security officials (anonymous)
a5001.speech: Said plans to deploy the roughly 500 U.S. forces in Somalia across the country to better support Danab are also under review now.

a5001.speaker: Senior Somali security official (anonymous)
a5001.name: Senior Somali security official (anonymous)
a5001.speech: Said an April 16 U.S. airstrike on two unflagged vessels off the Somali coast hit a shipment of surface-to-air missiles from Yemen.

a5001.speaker: U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM)
a5001.name: U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM)
a5001.speech: Declined to provide details, but its news release said the boat carried "advanced conventional weapons."

a5001.speaker: Western military official (anonymous)
a5001.name: Western military official (anonymous)
a5001.speech: "Airstrikes are only useful if you have good ground troops to hold."

a5001.speaker: Berkay Mandiraci, senior analyst for Turkey at the International Crisis Group
a5001.name: Berkay Mandiraci
a5001.title: senior analyst for Turkey at the International Crisis Group
a5001.speech: "With traditional powers retreating from parts of Africa, Ankara sees an opportunity to step in. Somalia holds strategic value for Ankara, sitting astride key shipping lanes and vital trade routes."

a5001.speaker: Other security partners of Somalia
a5001.name: Other security partners of Somalia
a5001.speech: Have said they are often not informed about Turkish operations.

a5001.speaker: Mogadishu-based diplomat (anonymous)
a5001.name: Mogadishu-based diplomat (anonymous)
a5001.speech: "At times you had multiple UAVs over a target."

a5001.speaker: Witnesses (to Turkish drone strikes)
a5001.name: Witnesses (to Turkish drone strikes)
a5001.speech: Told the Post that Turkish strikes from less-powerful drones have killed at least 40 civilians since late 2022; according to witnesses and a relative, a January 2023 strike on a gathering under a tree killed seven civilians, including an 8-year-old, in the town of Quracley.

a5001.speaker: Local doctor (Mubarak, Somalia)
a5001.name: Local doctor (Mubarak
a5001.title: Somalia)
a5001.speech: Said eight were killed on Sept. 9, 2022, when a strike hit a group of drivers and hawkers in the al-Shabab-controlled town of Mubarak.

a5001.speaker: Mohamed Nur Ahmed, 50, who lost three sons and a nephew in the Quracley strike
a5001.name: Mohamed Nur Ahmed
a5001.title: 50, who lost three sons and a nephew in the Quracley strike
a5001.speech: "I couldn't even wash my children's bodies according to the Islamic custom," because they were "ripped to pieces."

a5001.speaker: Western diplomat (anonymous)
a5001.name: Western diplomat (anonymous)
a5001.speech: "You've got the Somalis telling the Turks to … save Mogadishu at all costs. This will inevitably lead to further civilian casualties, which can be exploited by al-Shabab."

a5070.speaker: Imali Hermann Djetta, president of the National Chamber of Agriculture of Benin
a5070.name: Imali Hermann Djetta
a5070.title: president of the National Chamber of Agriculture of Benin
a5070.speech: Said the initiative aims at two main objectives: to present the opportunities for on-site processing of agricultural products offered by the Gdiz and the impact on job creation and the transformation of the Beninese economy, and to recall the rationale of the measures to preserve raw materials and the benefits for local and national economic development ; "Everything that concerns the agricultural world is of interest to the chamber of agriculture. Faced with this confirmed determination of the government, we thought it right that the producers should see what is happening." ; "Today, we know what they do with it and why they do it." ; "No one will come and develop our country in our place; it is we ourselves, and it is only through such acts that we can do it."

a5070.speaker: Aidath Mare, head of an NGO supporting women's cooperatives in soya and shea processing in northern Benin
a5070.name: Aidath Mare
a5070.title: head of an NGO supporting women's cooperatives in soya and shea processing in northern Benin
a5070.speech: "That it is Benin that today manufactures the threads, the towels, the uniforms of our police officers, customs officers and soldiers that we used to buy abroad -- it is wonderful, we are really happy." ; called on actors in the agricultural world to redouble their efforts in the production of cotton, soya and cashew: "It is a notable advance that must be saluted and it will transform our country," while thanking the government for the initiative of setting up the Gdiz.

a5070.speaker: Ali Deladi, president of the rice producers of the commune of Karimama
a5070.name: Ali Deladi
a5070.title: president of the rice producers of the commune of Karimama
a5070.speech: Promises to raise farmers' awareness about increasing production ; "We must serve our country before thinking about exporting. It is an achievement that we today process cashew, soya and cotton at home."

a5070.speaker: Oumarou Medawa, first deputy mayor of the commune of Karimama
a5070.name: Oumarou Medawa
a5070.title: first deputy mayor of the commune of Karimama
a5070.speech: Believes it is important that Beninese people understand that Benin is genuinely committed to industrial transformation ; "We visited the various processing factories and one can easily see that the cotton, the cashew, the soya that we produce in Benin are processed in this centre. We must understand that this is a centre which, beyond processing, creates jobs.
