That is to be saluted." ; said it was important to come and see, because many do not really know what is happening in the Glo-Djigbe industrial zone.

a5070.speaker: Letondji Beheton, managing director of Sipi Benin S.a.
a5070.name: Letondji Beheton
a5070.title: managing director of Sipi Benin S.a.
a5070.speech: Explained the processing that has been taking place in the business centre for 16 months; said the structural transformation desired for a new Benin means the industrialisation of the economy, moving from an economy based on exporting raw materials to one where they are processed for more added value, more wealth and more jobs ; "One cannot develop a country on the basis of foreign aid. What is needed instead is the mobilisation of resources, while having a strong economy. And a strong economy for Benin is an economy that will henceforth be based on the processing of our agricultural products." ; said all the factories installed in the zone use exclusively Beninese raw materials: "It is fitting that the producers realise what is being done with their raw materials. The transformation is real here. This zone is a representation of our country with all the languages that are spoken in it."

a5122.speaker: Virginia Palmer, US Ambassador to Ghana
a5122.name: Virginia Palmer
a5122.title: US Ambassador to Ghana
a5122.speech: Advised that contesting political parties must commit to a peace pact as soon as possible: "All political parties must sign the peace pact as soon as possible because that is a sure way to signal to the young people on the streets that violence in any form will not be the way to go during the elections" ; touted Ghana's democratic credentials, which she admitted were the envy of the rest of the continent and the world at large, and stressed the need for that to be jealously guarded during and after the crucial December 7 general election ; said elections were not battlegrounds or a period to make enemies but a platform to project ideas to the electorate for them to make a choice.

a5122.speaker: Virginia Palmer, US Ambassador to Ghana
a5122.name: Virginia Palmer
a5122.title: US Ambassador to Ghana
a5122.speech: Referenced the just-ended elections in the USA, which was won by former President Donald Trump over Vice-President Kamala Harris, and stated that immediately after the elections there had been business as usual in the US with all citizens living in peace; said no matter how violent the campaigns were, America emerged victorious and peaceful because the people believed it was where their power as citizens lay; urged Ghana to emulate that example as it had always been done since the Fourth Republic, to keep the peace, while remaining the beacon of democracy on the continent and beyond; expressed the hope that just as America had done it successfully, Ghana would also emerge victorious after the elections.

a5122.speaker: Joe Biden, US President (quoted by Ambassador Palmer)
a5122.name: Joe Biden
a5122.title: US President (quoted by Ambassador Palmer)
a5122.speech: "You can't love democracy only when you are winning and you can't love your neighbour only when you agree."

a5122.speaker: Ghana National Peace Council (as recalled by Ambassador Palmer)
a5122.name: Ghana National Peace Council (as recalled by Ambassador Palmer)
a5122.speech: Had been preaching that elections were not a battle between enemies but a contest of ideas between groups with different ideologies.

a5122.speaker: Virginia Palmer, US Ambassador to Ghana
a5122.name: Virginia Palmer
a5122.title: US Ambassador to Ghana
a5122.speech: Pledged the continuous support of America to Ghana, both politically and economically, as they strengthened the bond of friendship between the two countries.

a5122.speaker: John Agyekum Kufuor, former President of Ghana
a5122.name: John Agyekum Kufuor
a5122.title: former President of Ghana
a5122.speech: Called for greater partnership between Ghana and America in a manner that ensured a win-win for all and not one that was tilted against the other; recalled the enormous support Ghana enjoyed from the United States through the Millennium Challenge Account that resulted in the funding of some major road projects and the energy sector; expressed the hope that the bond of friendship between the two countries would extend way into the future in the interest of their citizens.

a5122.speaker: Kimathi Kuenyehia, President of the American Chamber of Commerce (AMCHAM) Ghana
a5122.name: Kimathi Kuenyehia
a5122.title: President of the American Chamber of Commerce (AMCHAM) Ghana
a5122.speech: Paid glowing tribute to the founder presidents, directors and patrons of AMCHAM, touting the benefits Ghanaian and American businesses have enjoyed in the last 35 years; said plans were afoot to have AMCHAM move from its rented premises into its own edifice, a project which would soon start.

a5233.speaker: Yonis Ali Guedi, Minister of Energy in charge of Natural Resources of Djibouti, and Lloyd Jackson, USAID representative
a5233.name: Yonis Ali Guedi
a5233.title: Minister of Energy in charge of Natural Resources of Djibouti, and Lloyd Jackson, USAID representative
a5233.speech: welcomed the excellence of relations between the two countries, hailing the USAID/MERN partnership.

a5237.speaker: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda, Minister of Health of Malawi
a5237.name: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda
a5237.title: Minister of Health of Malawi
a5237.speech: has assured Malawians that the country has sufficient stocks of HIV/AIDS drugs to last for at least 11 months, dismissing fears that the suspension of USAID funding could disrupt treatment and care; speaking on the sidelines of the 74th Health Ministers Conference of the ECSA Health Community in Lilongwe, she reaffirmed the government's commitment to ensuring uninterrupted healthcare services ; "We have continued to provide services as usual. Where USAID has withdrawn staff, we have deployed our own health workers to fill the gaps" ; she emphasized that Malawi has adequate stocks to manage HIV/AIDS treatment for the next 11 months, adding that the government is utilizing the Health Sector Joint Fund—supported by Germany, Norway, and the United Kingdom—to bridge financial shortfalls left by USAID's funding suspension ; reassured the public not to panic, stating that the government is actively engaging other development partners to ensure continuity in the health sector.

a5237.speaker: 74th Health Ministers Conference of the East, Central and Southern Africa Health Community (ECSA-HC)
a5237.name: 74th Health Ministers Conference of the East
a5237.title: Central and Southern Africa Health Community (ECSA-HC)
a5237.speech: downplayed the potential impact of the USAID funding suspension, citing ECSA-HC's cost-effective operational model.

a5237.speaker: Sibusiso Sibandze, ECSA-HC Acting Director-General
a5237.name: Sibusiso Sibandze
a5237.title: ECSA-HC Acting Director-General
a5237.speech: stressed in an interview that while USAID funding has been valuable, the organization implements its activities efficiently ; "Even with the funding withdrawal, we are confident in our ability to continue supporting member states."

a5237.speaker: Donald Trump, former U.S. President (executive order)
a5237.name: Donald Trump
a5237.title: former U.S. President (executive order)
a5237.speech: issued an executive order temporarily halting funding to certain developing nations, including Malawi, which USAID's withdrawal follows.

a5237.speaker: Michael Usi, Vice-President of Malawi
a5237.name: Michael Usi
a5237.title: Vice-President of Malawi
a5237.speech: who presided over the opening of the conference, urged member states to prioritize health data integration and adopt innovative financing strategies to strengthen regional health systems.

a5299.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
a5299.name: Donald Trump
a5299.title: U.S. President
a5299.speech: made the claim of a 'genocide' against white farmers in South Africa at a formal diplomatic meeting in the White House on 21 May; among the so-called evidence presented by Mr Trump to support the assertion was a video including footage purportedly of a 'mass funeral' for the white victims of farm attacks.

a5299.speaker: Two independent inquiries (one instituted by then police minister Steve Tshwete; the second by the South African Human Rights Commission)
a5299.name: Two independent inquiries (one instituted by then police minister Steve Tshwete; the second by the South African Human Rights Commission)
a5299.speech: Both investigated claims that attacks on farms and smallholdings were part of a political campaign to force white farmers off their land. Neither inquiry, nor other credible police or private investigations since then, have found any evidence to support such allegations.

a5299.speaker: 1948 Genocide Convention and the 1998 Rome Statute
a5299.name: 1948 Genocide Convention and the 1998 Rome Statute
a5299.speech: define genocide as murder or other harmful acts intended to destroy, in whole or in part, an ethnic group.

a5299.speaker: AfriForum study (of farm attack cases between 2016 and 2021)
a5299.name: AfriForum study (of farm attack cases between 2016 and 2021)
a5299.speech: revealed that only 18% resulted in a conviction.

a5299.speaker: South African Police Service (statistics)
a5299.name: South African Police Service (statistics)
a5299.speech: the South African Police Service's ability to detect murder nationally dropped by 65 per cent since 2012 and as of last year, stood at 11 per cent. Over the past five years, the conviction rate for murder nationally was just 13 per cent.

a5299.speaker: AfriForum (recorded figures)
a5299.name: AfriForum (recorded figures)
a5299.speech: in the 2023-24 financial year, the 49 murders on farms recorded by AfriForum represented 0.2 per cent of the 27,621 murders suffered nationally. And the 296 farm attacks recorded by AfriForum made up 0.7 per cent of the 42,206 robberies recorded by police across the country. While murders increased by 127 cases nationally from the previous year, AfriForum recorded a drop in one case from 50 to 49 for those occurring on farms.

a5299.speaker: National Rural Safety Strategy (South African government document)
a5299.name: National Rural Safety Strategy (South African government document)
a5299.speech: acknowledges that the government must improve safety, including in rural areas; however, the strategy has not been fully implemented, with resource and infrastructure shortages among the challenges.

a5299.speaker: David Lane, late US neo-Nazi and convicted criminal, in his 1988 book White Genocide Manifesto
a5299.name: David Lane
a5299.title: late US neo-Nazi and convicted criminal, in his 1988 book White Genocide Manifesto
a5299.speech: popularised the theory that white South Africans face a genocide.

a5513.speaker: Joakim Reiter, Vodafone Foundation's Chief External & Corporate Affairs Officer
a5513.name: Joakim Reiter
a5513.title: Vodafone Foundation's Chief External & Corporate Affairs Officer
a5513.speech: Expressed the significance of this expansion, saying, “The extension of m-mama to Malawi is a major milestone in our efforts to improve maternal health in sub-Saharan Africa. We are confident that this initiative will make a lasting impact on the lives of women and children.”

a5513.speaker: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda, Minister of Health of Malawi
a5513.name: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda
a5513.title: Minister of Health of Malawi
a5513.speech: Expressed the government's strong support for m-mama, highlighting the need for innovative solutions to reduce maternal deaths: “This initiative comes at a critical time, and we are fully committed to making sure it succeeds in Malawi. It will save lives, particularly in rural areas where access to healthcare has been a challenge for years.”

a5513.speaker: Dr. Mary Phiri, maternal health expert in Lilongwe
a5513.name: Dr. Mary Phiri
a5513.title: maternal health expert in Lilongwe
a5513.speech: “We have long struggled with maternal mortality, especially in rural areas where women face significant delays in getting to health facilities. The m-mama service will help solve that problem and save many lives.”

a5616.speaker: Nigerian government and UNDP’s “Imagine Nigeria” report
a5616.name: Nigerian government and UNDP’s “Imagine Nigeria” report
a5616.speech: according to the report, the country’s green economy is worth about $250 billion, with plastic recycling playing a central role, and boasting an estimated market size of $40 billion.

a5616.speaker: Lagos State Waste Management Authority (2021 report)
a5616.name: Lagos State Waste Management Authority (2021 report)
a5616.speech: indicated that the recycling economy of the state generated as much as 18 billion naira.

a5616.speaker: Experts
a5616.name: Experts
a5616.speech: estimate that a well-managed waste management system in Nigeria could create over 250,000 jobs by 2025.

a5666.speaker: Josefa Correia Sacko, African Union Commissioner for Agriculture, Rural Development, Blue Economy and Sustainable Environment
a5666.name: Josefa Correia Sacko
a5666.title: African Union Commissioner for Agriculture, Rural Development, Blue Economy and Sustainable Environment
a5666.speech: Expressed this concern at the 33rd FAO Regional Conference for Africa, stressing that this figure is “rising dramatically” because of the overlapping of new crises ; reported that the statistics indicate around 282 million people in Africa (about 20 percent of the population) are undernourished, an increase of 57 million people since the start of the covid-19 pandemic ; “We therefore need urgent and comprehensive action, since Africa is facing an unprecedented food crisis, which worsens every year due to the overlapping of new crises”, she stressed in her communication addressed to Inforpress.

a5666.speaker: Josefa Correia Sacko, African Union Commissioner for Agriculture, Rural Development, Blue Economy and Sustainable Environment
a5666.name: Josefa Correia Sacko
a5666.title: African Union Commissioner for Agriculture, Rural Development, Blue Economy and Sustainable Environment
a5666.speech: Argued that, to remedy this ill which is reaching “alarming proportions” on the continent, priority should go to promoting better production, broad processing and the use of native foods through intensified investment in research, as well as safeguarding relevant biodiversity, including mechanization throughout the food value chain ; said these orphan crops, including non-timber food products that make up Africa’s main staples, should be considered “opportunity crops” ; noted this strategy is in line with the “Vision for Adapted Crops and Soils” strategy launched jointly and very recently by the AU, FAO, USAID and other partners, the Common African Agro-Parks ; pointed out that another urgent action is the effective operationalization of the framework for sustainable agricultural mechanization in Africa (F-SAMA), including technology adapted to the needs of smallholder farmers, in particular women and young people ; reiterated the collaboration between the AU and the FAO and highlighted support for implementing the African Continental Free Trade Agreement, especially the promotion of agricultural trade to achieve food sovereignty by reducing food imports in Africa.

a5666.speaker: African regional overview of food security and nutrition – statistics and trends 2023 (report)
a5666.name: African regional overview of food security and nutrition – statistics and trends 2023 (report)
a5666.speech: Indicates that around 282 million people in Africa (about 20 percent of the population) are undernourished, an increase of 57 million people since the beginning of the covid-19 pandemic.

a5876.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a5876.name: Marco Rubio
a5876.title: US Secretary of State
a5876.speech: Told reporters he was now the acting head of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID); calling USAID "a completely unresponsive agency", said a lot of functions of the organisation "are going to continue" and "They're going to be part of American foreign policy, but it has to be aligned with American foreign policy."

a5876.speaker: Democratic lawmakers
a5876.name: Democratic lawmakers
a5876.speech: Have called it an "illegal, unconstitutional" move that would hurt poor people abroad, harm national security and reduce US influence on the global stage; outside USAID offices said the moves were against the law and that shuttering the agency would harm national security.

a5876.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5876.name: Donald Trump
a5876.title: US President
a5876.speech: Speaking to reporters at the White House on Monday, alleged the agency run by "radical left lunatics" was getting away with "tremendous fraud", but did not provide names or details.

a5876.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5876.name: Donald Trump
a5876.title: US President
a5876.speech: Defended Musk's handling of the situation, saying the tech tycoon has "access only to letting people go that he thinks are no good, if we agree with him, and it's only if we agree with him"; "Elon can't do and won't do anything without our approval."

a5876.speaker: Chris Van Hollen, US Senator (Maryland)
a5876.name: Chris Van Hollen
a5876.title: US Senator (Maryland)
a5876.speech: "It's not only a gift to our adversaries... it is plain illegal."

a5876.speaker: Johnny Olszewski, Maryland Congressman
a5876.name: Johnny Olszewski
a5876.title: Maryland Congressman
a5876.speech: Cited reports that prison guards in Syria responsible for containing thousands of Islamic State fighters nearly walked off the job after the earlier freeze on US aid: "This is real life, this is dangerous and this is serious."

a5876.speaker: Chris Murphy, US Senator (Connecticut)
a5876.name: Chris Murphy
a5876.title: US Senator (Connecticut)
a5876.speech: Claimed "Elon Musk makes billions of dollars based off of his business with China, and China is cheering at this action today."

a5876.speaker: Elon Musk, Trump adviser and head of the Department of Government Efficiency (Doge)
a5876.name: Elon Musk
a5876.title: Trump adviser and head of the Department of Government Efficiency (Doge)
a5876.speech: Posted dozens of messages over the weekend alleging the agency was rife with fraud and corruption, calling USAID "evil", a "criminal organisation" and a "radical-left political psy op" on X; in a live stream on X early Monday told followers: "You've got to basically get rid of the whole thing. It's beyond repair. ... We're shutting it down."

a5876.speaker: Katie Miller, Doge spokesperson
a5876.name: Katie Miller
a5876.title: Doge spokesperson
a5876.speech: Wrote on X: "No classified material was accessed without proper security clearances."

a5876.speaker: Internal USAID message obtained by the BBC
a5876.name: Internal USAID message obtained by the BBC
a5876.speech: Indicated hundreds of employees were locked out of their email.

a5876.speaker: US media citing unnamed White House sources
a5876.name: US media citing unnamed White House sources
a5876.speech: Said Musk had been given an unpaid job as a part-time "special government employee", a status which would potentially make him subject to several rules about financial disclosures and conflicts of interest.

a5876.speaker: The Washington Post and CNN
a5876.name: The Washington Post and CNN
a5876.speech: Reported that top officials have been placed on leave or resigned in the last several days following clashes with Musk's Doge, including over requests that employees of the unofficial department be given access to a highly secure area used for reviewing classified information; the Washington Post reported that USAID chief of staff Matt Hopson, a top political appointee, also resigned.

a5876.speaker: CBS
a5876.name: CBS
a5876.speech: Reports that USAID director for security John Vorhees and deputy Director for Security Brian McGill were both placed on administrative leave as a result.

a5927.speaker: Thabo Mbeki, President of South Africa and new SADC chairman
a5927.name: Thabo Mbeki
a5927.title: President of South Africa and new SADC chairman
a5927.speech: Urged SADC countries to utilise the Free Trade Area to achieve economic growth and integration in the region ; also called on SADC countries to become active players in the global economic arena which he said was dominated by countries such as China, India and the Americas, among others.

a6014.speaker: Roads Authority (RA)
a6014.name: Roads Authority (RA)
a6014.speech: Confirmed having information that the rains have damaged Mangochi-Monkey Bay Road, Golomoti-Monkey Bay Road, the M5 cut-off at Pengapenga in Ntcheu and Chapananga Road in Chikwawa.

a6014.speaker: Ammiel Champiti, Roads Authority chief executive officer
a6014.name: Ammiel Champiti
a6014.title: Roads Authority chief executive officer
a6014.speech: Said they are assessing the extent of damage on the roads so that they should work on the affected ones within the week: "The repair works will be conducted to ensure that there is no continued disconnection between the affected places."

a6014.speaker: Bishop Witmos, Mangochi District Council spokesperson
a6014.name: Bishop Witmos
a6014.title: Mangochi District Council spokesperson
a6014.speech: Said the affected households are in urgent need of humanitarian assistance as they have lost their houses, crops, livestock and other properties: "The situation is bad and terrible. The council has established the shelters just to give the affected people refuge while we are thinking of ways of supporting them."

a6014.speaker: Agnes Mbewe, 47, flood survivor from T/A Chimwala in Mangochi
a6014.name: Agnes Mbewe
a6014.title: 47, flood survivor from T/A Chimwala in Mangochi
a6014.speech: Said she managed to escape with her children when their house collapsed.

a6014.speaker: Aisha Mambo Adams, Mangochi Nkungulu legislator (United Democratic Front) and Second Deputy Speaker of Parliament
a6014.name: Aisha Mambo Adams
a6014.title: Mangochi Nkungulu legislator (United Democratic Front) and Second Deputy Speaker of Parliament
a6014.speech: Has called for immediate intervention from the government and humanitarian organisations: "This is a tragedy, and our people are suffering. We urgently need food, clean water, medical supplies, and proper sanitation in these camps. I am engaging authorities to ensure that relief items reach the affected families as soon as possible."

a6014.speaker: Maston Kaiya, Ntcheu District spokesperson
a6014.name: Maston Kaiya
a6014.title: Ntcheu District spokesperson
a6014.speech: Said rains have also damaged crops belonging to 1 779 farmers in Chawanje, Mphoola, and Chikadya in the district.

a6014.speaker: People in Nsanje
a6014.name: People in Nsanje
a6014.speech: Complained last week that they were not accessing services at Mbenje Health Centre after floods affected the health facility.

a6014.speaker: Department of Disaster Management Affairs (data)
a6014.name: Department of Disaster Management Affairs (data)
a6014.speech: Data shows that as of January 21 2025, severe weather characterised by heavy rains had cumulatively killed 31 people, injured 382 and affected 31 413 others since the start of the 2024/25 rainfall season.

a6033.speaker: John Charuk S. Siafa, Monrovia City Mayor
a6033.name: John Charuk S. Siafa
a6033.title: Monrovia City Mayor
a6033.speech: Says the Monrovia City Corporation (MCC) is seeking both local and international partners' help to strengthen Liberia's waste management system ; stressed the urgent need for investment in sustainable waste solutions, noting that it requires significant funding: "We are looking for partners to invest in the sector so it can be used either for electricity generation or for recycling purposes."

a6033.speaker: John Charuk S. Siafa, Monrovia City Mayor
a6033.name: John Charuk S. Siafa
a6033.title: Monrovia City Mayor
a6033.speech: Said the MCC recently placed advertisements in local newspapers inviting proposals from companies interested in waste management initiatives, and that several proposals have already been received and are currently under review: "We are now evaluating the proposals to identify the most suitable candidates, who will be announced very soon" ; revealed that a Liberian company has made it to the shortlist of the tendering process: "We know it will take time, but we believe we will get there."

a6033.speaker: John Charuk S. Siafa, Monrovia City Mayor
a6033.name: John Charuk S. Siafa
a6033.title: Monrovia City Mayor
a6033.speech: Reiterated that the MCC continues to seek more investors to provide substantial support that will truly transform waste into a resource in Liberia: "Whatever we do, Liberians involved in waste management including CBEs and SMBs will be at the forefront. We hope they will also be willing to take full part in this initiative."

a6033.speaker: John Charuk S. Siafa, Monrovia City Mayor
a6033.name: John Charuk S. Siafa
a6033.title: Monrovia City Mayor
a6033.speech: Said the MCC has allocated one million dollars in its budget with the national government for city cleaning, aimed at decentralizing waste collection across Monrovia and its surroundings: "We have already engaged the Ministry of Finance, and, for the first time, we've developed a strategy to use this budget to acquire equipment for all townships and districts commissioner so they can collaborate directly with MCC in collecting the waste" ; "Once the government releases the necessary funds, we will be able to give even greater support" ; mentioned plans to introduce door to door waste collection services, noting that investor support is essential for expanding and maintaining such a program.

a6033.speaker: John Charuk S. Siafa, Monrovia City Mayor
a6033.name: John Charuk S. Siafa
a6033.title: Monrovia City Mayor
a6033.speech: According to Mayor Siafa, countries like China, amongst other partners, have already pledged donations that include fire trucks, scholarships, and other equipment, which are expected to arrive in the country soon.

a6157.speaker: Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System (ACARS) data from MS804
a6157.name: Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System (ACARS) data from MS804
a6157.speech: Data from MS804's ACARS detected that smoke alarms had been triggered minutes before signal with the aircraft was lost approximately 16km within Egyptian airspace.

a6157.speaker: Some civil aviation experts
a6157.name: Some civil aviation experts
a6157.speech: The fragmentation of the debris and human remains led some civil aviation experts to suggest that an explosion may have occurred aboard the aircraft.

a6157.speaker: Semi-official Islamic State (IS) social media accounts
a6157.name: Semi-official Islamic State (IS) social media accounts
a6157.speech: Claimed the October 2015 downing of Metrojet flight 9268, en route from Sharm el-Sheikh (Egypt) to Saint Petersburg (Russia), hours after the crash was confirmed.

a6157.speaker: Stratfor, global intelligence firm
a6157.name: Stratfor
a6157.title: global intelligence firm
a6157.speech: In its post-mortem of the Egyptian airliner's crash, Stratfor references the 1994 downing of Philippine Airlines Flight 434 by an improvised explosive device (IED) comprised of components concealed in items such as modified shoe heels and a digital watch.

a6157.speaker: Islamic State (IS), in its English propaganda magazine Dabiq (12th edition)
a6157.name: Islamic State (IS)
a6157.title: in its English propaganda magazine Dabiq (12th edition)
a6157.speech: The group disclosed that it downed Metrojet 9286 via an IED which has since become known as the Schweppes bomb.

a6180.speaker: Assitan Coulibaly, President of the Malian Red Cross, and Dorien Irene Dolman, International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
a6180.name: Assitan Coulibaly
a6180.title: President of the Malian Red Cross, and Dorien Irene Dolman, International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
a6180.speech: "The Malian Red Cross needs 5 billion 600 million CFA francs to provide integrated relief assistance and alleviate the suffering of 200,000 people in Mali during 2025" ; said that in less than three weeks the Malian Red Cross has already mobilised more than 800 million CFA francs: "We are hoping for generous donors for the rest."

a6180.speaker: Officials of the Malian Red Cross
a6180.name: Officials of the Malian Red Cross
a6180.speech: Said more than 1.3 million people are affected and are in a situation of food insecurity because of conflicts and the security crisis; among them 120,000 people are in an emergency situation; the situation has been aggravated by floods that affected 370,000 people and displaced thousands of families.

a6180.speaker: Nouhoum Maiga, Secretary General of the Red Cross in Mali
a6180.name: Nouhoum Maiga
a6180.title: Secretary General of the Red Cross in Mali
a6180.speech: Considers that this situation will create a complex humanitarian crisis which must be addressed in time.

a6180.speaker: Dr Boubacar Niare, head of the disaster management department at the Red Cross in Mali
a6180.name: Dr Boubacar Niare
a6180.title: head of the disaster management department at the Red Cross in Mali
a6180.speech: Said that with these 5 and a half billion the Malian Red Cross intends to intervene in Bamako and in 7 regions of Mali - "Kayes, Koulikoro, Segou, Mopti, Sikasso, Timbuktu and Gao" - specifying actions such as the provision of shelter, income-generating activities and sanitary and hygiene kits to families, and also in the field of education.

a6180.speaker: Dr Abdoulaye Guindo, Secretary General of the Ministry of Health and Social Development
a6180.name: Dr Abdoulaye Guindo
a6180.title: Secretary General of the Ministry of Health and Social Development
a6180.speech: Launched the Red Cross response plan in these terms: "This response that we are putting in place today will determine the future of thousands of families and people affected in Mali. I hereby declare this response plan launched."

a6267.speaker: Nicolo Machiavelli (advice to “The Prince”)
a6267.name: Nicolo Machiavelli (advice to “The Prince”)
a6267.speech: “it is better to be feared than to be loved if one cannot be both.”

a6267.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a6267.name: Donald Trump
a6267.title: President of the United States
a6267.speech: Has consistently accused Canada and Mexico of being ‘’bad trade partners” who have not treated America right; complained that the “unfair” trade deficit with Canada is between $200 billion and $250 billion ; speaking recently at the World Economic Forum in Davos, made it clear that he doesn’t “need Canadian cars, lumber or oil”.

a6267.speaker: Pierre Trudeau, former Prime Minister of Canada
a6267.name: Pierre Trudeau
a6267.title: former Prime Minister of Canada
a6267.speech: Said in 1969 of relations with the US, “Living next to you, is in some ways, like sleeping with an elephant. No matter how friendly and even-tempered is the beast, if I can call it that, one is affected by every twitch and grunt.”

a6267.speaker: analysts
a6267.name: analysts
a6267.speech: Say that much of the deficit was “caused by the U.S. importing Canadian oil, which keeps costs at the pump down for Americans.”

a6267.speaker: Trump’s aides
a6267.name: Trump’s aides
a6267.speech: Argue that tariffs are either being used as a “negotiating tool” or a “means of raising taxes on foreigners to pay for retaining low tax rates on Americans.”

a6267.speaker: Stephen Miran, previous senior Trump adviser nominated to chair the Council of Economic Advisers (paper)
a6267.name: Stephen Miran
a6267.title: previous senior Trump adviser nominated to chair the Council of Economic Advisers (paper)
a6267.speech: In a paper touted to serve as a blueprint for Trump 2.0, anchors a proposal to reform the global trading system on the proviso “that access to the U.S. consumer market is a privilege that must be earned, not a right.”

a6267.speaker: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, WTO Director-General
a6267.name: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
a6267.title: WTO Director-General
a6267.speech: Has called for dialogue and restraint among members in response to the Trump phenomenon; drawing parallels to the 1930s Smoot-Hawley Act, warns that retaliatory trade wars could have catastrophic consequences for global growth.

a6267.speaker: Giulio Gallarotti
a6267.name: Giulio Gallarotti
a6267.speech: Argues that unilateralism “can be especially debilitating, because in an interdependent and globalised world, unilateral solutions to international problems are often inferior to collective solutions” ; submits that “…forsaking erstwhile allies and international commitments in favour of unilateral solutions produces a maverick image that compromises traditional sources of power embedded in multilateral support networks. Without such networks, even preponderant national resources will fall short of the effectiveness of multilateral solutions in attending to foreign objectives, thus creating an unsupportable burden for the maverick nation.”

a6267.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a6267.name: Donald Trump
a6267.title: President of the United States
a6267.speech: On the withdrawal of the United States from the World Health Organization: “World Health ripped us off, everybody rips off the United States. It’s not going to happen anymore.”

a6267.speaker: Lawrence Gostin, professor of global health at Georgetown University
a6267.name: Lawrence Gostin
a6267.title: professor of global health at Georgetown University
a6267.speech: “This is the darkest day for global health I have ever experienced…Trump could be sowing the seeds for the next pandemic.”

a6267.speaker: The White House
a6267.name: The White House
a6267.speech: Celebrated the “victory” in the standoff with Colombia as evidence that the US is “respected again”.

a6267.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a6267.name: Donald Trump
a6267.title: President of the United States
a6267.speech: Describing DeepSeek: “…a wake-up call for our industries that we need to be laser-focused on competing”.

a6267.speaker: Mike Johnson, House Speaker
a6267.name: Mike Johnson
a6267.title: House Speaker
a6267.speech: DeepSeek is “a serious threat” from China, which is a “terrible trading partner.” “They abuse the system. They steal our intellectual property. They’re now trying to get a leg up on us on AI, as you’ve seen the last day or so… It’s a serious threat to us and to our economy and our security in every way.”

a6267.speaker: Joseph Nye Jr.
a6267.name: Joseph Nye Jr.
a6267.speech: Explains, “…in a world where borders are becoming more porous than ever to everything from drugs to infectious diseases to terrorism, nations must mobilize international coalitions and build institutions to address shared threats and challenges. In this sense, power becomes a positive-sum game. It is not enough to think in terms of power over others. We must also think in terms of power to accomplish goals that involves power with others. On many transnational issues, empowering others can help us to accomplish our own goals. In this world, networks and connectedness become an important source of relevant power”.

a6267.speaker: An Australian Senator (placard)
a6267.name: An Australian Senator (placard)
a6267.speech: “…if you respect the world’s laws, the world will respect you.”

a6305.speaker: Bloomberg
a6305.name: Bloomberg
a6305.speech: Reported that the European Union will review its foreign aid programme, worth billions of Euros, in order to align the distribution of those funds more closely with its foreign policy interests ; reported, according to draft documents, that the European Commission will pause the disbursement of foreign aid and make it "more targeted towards partners" ; said that in the coming weeks the European Commission will set out its ideas for improving its budget for the next seven years, from 2028 to 2034.

a6305.speaker: The White House (Ikulu ya Marekani)
a6305.name: The White House (Ikulu ya Marekani)
a6305.speech: Has repeatedly accused USAID of waste and fraud, although foreign aid accounts for only one percent of the federal budget.

a6305.speaker: Tanzanian experts and civil society operators
a6305.name: Tanzanian experts and civil society operators
a6305.speech: Have proposed various steps these organisations can take to continue their activities and secure their sustainability.

a6305.speaker: Dr John Kalage, Executive Director of HakiElimu
a6305.name: Dr John Kalage
a6305.title: Executive Director of HakiElimu
a6305.speech: Told The Citizen that Tanzanian companies should consider supporting and investing in civil society organisations and NGOs to ensure they survive; the government should set aside a development budget for civil society organisations so that they can continue to exist ; "It is the right time and a call for the Government to look for domestic funds to support its development projects instead of depending on aid, concessional loans, and external funding" ; "International institutions that have not changed their position on withdrawing aid should also consider giving us cash instead, so that we can invest in sustainable projects and achieve long-term resilience."

a6305.speaker: Salim Awadh, business capital expert
a6305.name: Salim Awadh
a6305.title: business capital expert
a6305.speech: "I have said many times that, if NGOs do not change their funding model, they will disappear one after another. As I have said many times, 96 percent of NGOs in Tanzania are not financially sustainable."

a6344.speaker: National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) of Senegal (press release)
a6344.name: National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) of Senegal (press release)
a6344.speech: Expressed, this Friday, its deep concern over the situation of Senegalese nationals in Mayotte, who were hard hit by the passage of Cyclone Chido.

a6344.speaker: National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) of Senegal (press release)
a6344.name: National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) of Senegal (press release)
a6344.speech: Issued an urgent appeal for mobilisation in order to provide immediate humanitarian aid meeting the essential needs of the victims; also calls for stepping up the intervention of the Senegalese authorities, with a view to protecting and supporting Senegalese nationals in Mayotte, in coordination with the diplomatic and consular missions; urges that respect for human rights be guaranteed, while ensuring that the dignity, safety and health of the affected persons are preserved.

a6344.speaker: National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) of Senegal (press release)
a6344.name: National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) of Senegal (press release)
a6344.speech: Expressed its solidarity with all the populations affected by this tragedy, while paying tribute to the victims and offering its condolences to the bereaved families; and invited citizens to report any worrying situation.

a6408.speaker: Max Cuvellier Giacomelli, head of mobile development at the GSMA
a6408.name: Max Cuvellier Giacomelli
a6408.title: head of mobile development at the GSMA
a6408.speech: "From our experience, we have seen how the right technical assistance can truly help companies unlock impact at scale" ; "Through this new round, we believe we can deepen the private sector's contribution to the closing of the gender divide across low- and middle-income countries, in line with the GSMA Foundation's unwavering commitment to addressing this challenge."

a6542.speaker: Primate Elijah Ayodele, Founder and Leader of INRI Spiritual Evangelical Church
a6542.name: Primate Elijah Ayodele
a6542.title: Founder and Leader of INRI Spiritual Evangelical Church
a6542.speech: Prophesied in a video made in September 2023 regarding Botswana, held on several occasions long before the election that the incumbent president would be disappointed at the election polls and that the outcome would be shocking and disappointing to the ruling party: “The incumbent president of Botswana must pray for good health and God’s divine help. The country should pray against disease outbreaks and the prevention of border crises. The president will have a tough time because he will shoot himself with an unpopular policy. I see their currency becoming weaker. Investors will dump the country. They need to be careful of external attack, the president will be betrayed.”

a6542.speaker: Primate Elijah Ayodele, Founder and Leader of INRI Spiritual Evangelical Church
a6542.name: Primate Elijah Ayodele
a6542.title: Founder and Leader of INRI Spiritual Evangelical Church
a6542.speech: Warned Kamala Harris of her loss of the US presidential election; foretold the emergence of Donald Trump in 2016 and his loss in 2020, the incapability of Joe Biden, and the re-emergence of Donald Trump as president of the United States of America.

a6542.speaker: Primate Elijah Ayodele, Founder and Leader of INRI Spiritual Evangelical Church
a6542.name: Primate Elijah Ayodele
a6542.title: Founder and Leader of INRI Spiritual Evangelical Church
a6542.speech: Prophesied the emergence of a new terrorist group in Nigeria; also correctly prophesied the loss of the Mauritius election by the incumbent.

a6542.speaker: Nigerian military
a6542.name: Nigerian military
a6542.speech: Confirmed that a new terrorist group, ‘Lukarawas’, has emerged in the North-western part of the country.

a6542.speaker: Primate Elijah Ayodele, Founder and Leader of INRI Spiritual Evangelical Church (statement released by his media aide, Osho Oluwatosin, 21 September 2023)
a6542.name: Primate Elijah Ayodele
a6542.title: Founder and Leader of INRI Spiritual Evangelical Church (statement released by his media aide, Osho Oluwatosin, 21 September 2023)
a6542.speech: Warned Governor Godwin Obaseki to be careful in his fight against the former deputy governor, Phillip Shaibu, calling on him to stealth his sword because fighting him would make PDP lose the election, and advising him to be more diplomatic and focus on winning: “Obaseki should stealth his sword, fighting his deputy will make him fail. He should be more diplomatic about this matter. I warned you that you and your deputy will fight three years ago and it will lead to your political weakness. Fighting him will make PDP lose, if there are issues, come together and sort it. Don’t wash your dirty linen outside. This fight will not give you victory, it will make you lose, stop fighting.” ; “The fight is going more spiritual and it may affect PDP chances in the coming election. The party can lose in Edo if this fight continues. Instead of putting your house together and see how you will win the election, you are fighting. Stop this fight. There’s more to do than the fight. It’s a small world, look at the beginning, don’t let it make you lose the state; don’t think your people love you. Those clapping for you will be the ones that will create problems for you.”

a6542.speaker: Primate Elijah Ayodele, Founder and Leader of INRI Spiritual Evangelical Church
a6542.name: Primate Elijah Ayodele
a6542.title: Founder and Leader of INRI Spiritual Evangelical Church
a6542.speech: Foretold the arrest of Simon Ekpa, a Finnish-Nigerian separatist agitator and self-proclaimed Prime Minister of the Biafra Republic Government In-Exile.

a6838.speaker: Onalethata Mpebe, founder of Positive Moments organisation
a6838.name: Onalethata Mpebe
a6838.title: founder of Positive Moments organisation
a6838.speech: “We have seen people turn their lives around. But now, that support is slipping away. These are not just services. These are people's lives.” ; “We made sure that people’s voices were heard” ; “But now, without funding, we can’t continue this work. It’s devastating.” ; “These services are crucial for mothers, young girls, and even foreigners who rely on us” ; “Without these programmes, so many people will fall through the cracks.”

a6838.speaker: Onalethata Mpebe, founder of Positive Moments organisation
a6838.name: Onalethata Mpebe
a6838.title: founder of Positive Moments organisation
a6838.speech: On the gap in HIV prevention and awareness and on stigma: “People think that by now, everyone knows about HIV, but that is not true. Many young girls don’t use protection, and some are in relationships with older men, which puts them at even higher risk.” ; “People are afraid to be seen going to clinics for treatment. Many have not told their families they have HIV because they fear being judged.”

a6838.speaker: Onalethata Mpebe, founder of Positive Moments organisation
a6838.name: Onalethata Mpebe
a6838.title: founder of Positive Moments organisation
a6838.speech: On the halt in PEPFAR funding leading to job losses and organisation closures: “We are talking about hundreds of people losing jobs, and communities losing access to care”, adding that, “Without funding, we are not only losing projects; we are losing people who were essential to the fight against HIV” ; “I have helped people who were too scared to start treatment, people who were ashamed of their status, and those who had given up. Without these programmes, many won’t get the help they need in time.”

a6838.speaker: Onalethata Mpebe, founder of Positive Moments organisation
a6838.name: Onalethata Mpebe
a6838.title: founder of Positive Moments organisation
a6838.speech: Warned that Botswana’s progress against HIV is in danger without PEPFAR: “Botswana was leading the fight, but now we are at risk of falling behind” ; “We are trying to become self-reliant, but this funding cut makes it much harder.” ; said she hopes to find new donors and explore different funding options, including crowdfunding: “We can’t give up. Too many people are depending on us.”

a6838.speaker: Onalethata Mpebe, founder of Positive Moments organisation
a6838.name: Onalethata Mpebe
a6838.title: founder of Positive Moments organisation
a6838.speech: Calling on the international community to step in: “We need help now more than ever. If we are going to end HIV by 2030, we can’t do it alone.” ; “Everyone can do something, no matter how small. We all have a role to play in ending HIV. Let’s come together to build stronger communities and fight for a future where no one has to fear HIV.”

a6838.speaker: A close friend who helped connect a young HIV-positive mother to Positive Moments (anonymous)
a6838.name: A close friend who helped connect a young HIV-positive mother to Positive Moments (anonymous)
a6838.speech: Testified: “She has been happy and accepted herself ever since” ; “She has even forgotten she ever cried about her diagnosis. Now we joke together.”

a6838.speaker: Another community member (anonymous)
a6838.name: Another community member (anonymous)
a6838.speech: Said Mpebe’s work made it easy for her to realise it is not the end of life; she was down on the day she was diagnosed, wondering how she would live and face people: “But through Mpebe, I saw there is life after HIV.”

a6917.speaker: Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF)
a6917.name: Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF)
a6917.speech: Denies the attack on the military camp and has accused Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed of concocting the story to justify deploying the military ; has been saying that there have been no air strike in the region, and later gave a contradicting statement accusing the federal government of air attacks and military operation in the region.

a6917.speaker: Federal government of Ethiopia
a6917.name: Federal government of Ethiopia
a6917.speech: Has said the National Air Force is attacking major possible targets.

a6917.speaker: Debretsion Gebremichael, President of the TPLF
a6917.name: Debretsion Gebremichael
a6917.title: President of the TPLF
a6917.speech: Said in his statement on Friday that the government had launched air strikes on Mekelle, Adigrat, Alamata, and parts of the western Tigray region and Shiraro ; "The war is not complete, this is just the beginning, more than 10,000 members of the Northern Command and Defense Forces currently are under the control of the Tigray National Regional State."

a6917.speaker: State of emergency fact check
a6917.name: State of emergency fact check
a6917.speech: Said that in the late hours of November 13, 2020, TPLF had fired a rocket towards Bahir Dar and Gondar cities, and that as a result the airport areas have sustained damages.

a6917.speaker: Tigray regional government
a6917.name: Tigray regional government
a6917.speech: Has accused Abiy's government of cooperating with Eritrea to attack the Tigray region and its people.

a6917.speaker: Eritrean government
a6917.name: Eritrean government
a6917.speech: Has announced it as a false accusation.

a6917.speaker: Tigray government (statement posted on its Facebook page)
a6917.name: Tigray government (statement posted on its Facebook page)
a6917.speech: Said it would win the "justified" war, and added that a fighter will not "negotiate with their enemies."

a6917.speaker: Debretsion Gebremichael, President of the TPLF
a6917.name: Debretsion Gebremichael
a6917.title: President of the TPLF
a6917.speech: Said in a letter sent to all political and civic stakeholders regarding the current affairs that problems cannot be solved through military means, and that the African Union has the responsibility to bring all political and civic stakeholders of the country into an all-inclusive and comprehensive dialogue.

a6917.speaker: Humanitarian partners
a6917.name: Humanitarian partners
a6917.speech: Have asked federal and regional authorities to facilitate humanitarian access to reach people in need in areas under their respective control.

a6917.speaker: Amhara regional state
a6917.name: Amhara regional state
a6917.speech: On Monday, November 9, announced a death toll of about 500 civilians in Mai-Kadra town in the South West Zone of Ethiopia's Tigray Region where both Tigray and Amhara natives live ; states the mass killing was ethnic based, where hundreds of Amhara people were selected to death.

a6917.speaker: Daniel Bekele, head of the Ethiopian Human Rights Commission
a6917.name: Daniel Bekele
a6917.title: head of the Ethiopian Human Rights Commission
a6917.speech: Informed Capital that the commission has sent a group of investigators to investigate the situation at Mai-Kadra and that the commission will compose reports and information to ensure accountability by investigating and gathering evidence of human rights violations committed by any party involved in the conflict ; "One of the concerns of the commission is working to protect civilians and non-participants on the war, and the commission is working closely with different stakeholders to insure civilian protection" ; "In the current context of the ongoing conflict in the Tigray region, it is important to ensure access to humanitarian assistance and basic services, especially for the safety and protection of civilians who are not involved in the conflict."

a6917.speaker: Ethiopian Human Rights Commission
a6917.name: Ethiopian Human Rights Commission
a6917.speech: "Therefore, the armed forces involved in the conflict have a responsibility to protect civilians," says the commission ; has said that it is closely following the government's crackdown on the conflict in various parts of the country and allegations of discrimination in some areas on the basis of ethnicity.

a6917.speaker: Amnesty International report (November 12)
a6917.name: Amnesty International report (November 12)
a6917.speech: Confirms that scores, and likely hundreds, of people were stabbed or hacked to death in Mai-Kadra ; the organization's Crisis Evidence Lab has examined and digitally verified gruesome photographs and videos of bodies strewn across the town or being carried away on stretchers, confirmed the images were recent using satellite imagery, and geo-located them to Mai-Kadra in western Tigray state.

a6917.speaker: Deprose Muchena, Amnesty International's Director for East and Southern Africa
a6917.name: Deprose Muchena
a6917.title: Amnesty International's Director for East and Southern Africa
a6917.speech: "We have confirmed the massacre of a very large number of civilians, who appear to have been day laborers who in no way are involved in the ongoing military offensive" ; "This is a horrific tragedy whose true extent only time will tell as communication in Tigray remains shut down."

a6917.speaker: Federal government of Ethiopia
a6917.name: Federal government of Ethiopia
a6917.speech: Has accused the TPLF of the massacre in the town for killing civilians ; "The TPLF is violating international child rights provisions and is barring even children from joining the Special Forces" ; is accusing TPLF criminal gangs of setting up executive networks in Addis Ababa and other parts of the country to instill fear by carrying out terrorist attacks.

a6917.speaker: Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF)
a6917.name: Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF)
a6917.speech: On Friday denied the accusation and the Amnesty report, arguing the direct and indirect culprits are the fascist and the terrorist "Abiy Ahmed" who declared war on the people of Tigray.

a6917.speaker: Federal police / Addis Ababa Police Commission
a6917.name: Federal police / Addis Ababa Police Commission
a6917.speech: Have announced that they have banned 14 private security agencies from operating illegally, saying that some private security agencies have recently been set up to carry out attacks on public and government institutions, as well as the recruitment and deployment of security forces, in defiance of their purpose, and that the Addis Ababa Police Commission, in collaboration with other security forces, seized 163 firearms, 1194 rounds of ammunition and other assets during a three-day search operation ; the federal police commission has issued an arrest warrant on officials of TPLF, the suspects said to have been involved in armed robbery, by attacking the national defense and other related crimes.

a6917.speaker: Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF)
a6917.name: Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF)
a6917.speech: After its announcement of taking control of Tekeze dam on Sunday, on Friday November 13 claimed that the federal government has bombed Tekeze Dam.

a6917.speaker: State of emergency task force
a6917.name: State of emergency task force
a6917.speech: Has said the information is false and accused them of peddling falsehood for an international audience.

a6917.speaker: UNHCR Sudan
a6917.name: UNHCR Sudan
a6917.speech: Reported that at least 3,400 Ethiopian asylum seekers have crossed the Sudanese border through two border entry points in Gedaref State since the 9th November, and that 1,700 people have so far been screened and registered.

a6917.speaker: Sudanese authorities
a6917.name: Sudanese authorities
a6917.speech: Said no armed individual will be allowed to cross into Sudan.

a6917.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a6917.name: Abiy Ahmed
a6917.title: Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a6917.speech: On Friday told Members of the Tigray Special Forces to surrender to the Defense Forces within the next three days.

a6917.speaker: Government statement (Saturday)
a6917.name: Government statement (Saturday)
a6917.speech: Confirmed that in the late hours of Nov. 13, a rocket was fired towards Bahir Dar and Gondar cities, that as a result the airport areas have sustained damages, and that details of the incident are currently under investigation.

a6969.speaker: Non-governmental organisations (NGOs) in Namibia
a6969.name: Non-governmental organisations (NGOs) in Namibia
a6969.speech: Have called for the establishment of a State fund to assist institutions which have lost funding from international donors.

a6969.speaker: Ministry of Health and Social Services (Namibia)
a6969.name: Ministry of Health and Social Services (Namibia)
a6969.speech: Revealed that 120 inactive NGOs will face deregistration, unless they submit their annual reports.

a6969.speaker: Sandi Tjaronda, chairperson of the NANGOF Trust
a6969.name: Sandi Tjaronda
a6969.title: chairperson of the NANGOF Trust
a6969.speech: Argued that African states should follow the example of European countries, and allocate budgets for NGOs. "In the rest of the world, NGOs are supported by the State or public resources. For instance, in Europe and the United States, NGOs receive support from the government. An example is PEPFAR, which is an NGO funded by the US government to implement programmes on behalf of the State."

a6969.speaker: Sandi Tjaronda, chairperson of the NANGOF Trust
a6969.name: Sandi Tjaronda
a6969.title: chairperson of the NANGOF Trust
a6969.speech: Said the institution has been redundant for almost 10 years after the European Union, which was the donor at that time, pulled out and they could not sustain their operations ; attributed NGOs' downfall to a lack of funds, lack of voluntarism and staff capacity, withdrawal of international donors, as well as Covid-19.

a6969.speaker: Ben Schernick, executive director of the Nutrition and Food Security Alliance of Namibia (NAFSAN)
a6969.name: Ben Schernick
a6969.title: executive director of the Nutrition and Food Security Alliance of Namibia (NAFSAN)
a6969.speech: "I completely support the idea, and we do need some form of a funding mechanism. But I think it should not be solely on the government to provide that. Government can contribute, but the private sector or other development partners would also need to contribute."

a6969.speaker: Ben Schernick, executive director of the Nutrition and Food Security Alliance of Namibia (NAFSAN)
a6969.name: Ben Schernick
a6969.title: executive director of the Nutrition and Food Security Alliance of Namibia (NAFSAN)
a6969.speech: Advised the government to consider social contracting, in which NGOs provide essential services, including social services and educational support, particularly for children with disabilities or malnutrition. "There are other affected groups and NGOs; NGOs which provide essential counselling services for issues related to gender-based violence (GBV). If the government requests these organisations to deliver certain services and allocates a budget for that, it could be very beneficial."

a6969.speaker: Veronica Haimbili, Country Coordinator of Gender Links
a6969.name: Veronica Haimbili
a6969.title: Country Coordinator of Gender Links
a6969.speech: Said proposals to support NGOs has become a necessity rather than just a viable option, a shift that is crucial especially now that many international donors have withdrawn their support based on Namibia's classification as a middle-income country ; maintained that NGOs play a vital role in Namibian communities, often serving as the eyes and ears of the government, and implementing crucial projects which would otherwise fall under the government's purview. "If we are serious about our country's development and committed to the principle of 'leaving no one behind,' government funding for NGOs emerges as the most effective option available."

a6969.speaker: Veronica Haimbili, Country Coordinator of Gender Links
a6969.name: Veronica Haimbili
a6969.title: Country Coordinator of Gender Links
a6969.speech: Said the Ministry of Health and Social Services' policy to contract NGOs, particularly for activities related to HIV and AIDS, is a progressive approach that should serve as a model for other government ministries and departments to follow. "I think that's a good idea because NGOs can support the government's agenda in their development plans, and can be a good partner to the government."

a6969.speaker: Kirsten Moeller Jensen, managing director of Development Aid from People to People (DAPP) Namibia
a6969.name: Kirsten Moeller Jensen
a6969.title: managing director of Development Aid from People to People (DAPP) Namibia
a6969.speech: Opined that NGOs could support the government in achieving development plans and goals.

a7005.speaker: Namibian Ministry of Mines and Energy (monthly fuel price review)
a7005.name: Namibian Ministry of Mines and Energy (monthly fuel price review)
a7005.speech: Cites increasing crude oil prices that have been influenced by various geopolitical and economic factors: "The sanctions and geopolitical tensions affecting major oil-producing countries, and OPEC+ production cuts, have led to a reduction in the global oil supply, fuelling higher prices. The current increased oil demand, particularly in the northern hemisphere due to winter effects, has also played a significant role in driving fuel prices up" ; added that currency exchange rate fluctuations between the Namibia and US dollar also impacted the decision to increase fuel prices, considering the Namibia dollar depreciated 2.9% against the US dollar since the end of December 2024.

a7005.speaker: Namibian Ministry of Mines and Energy
a7005.name: Namibian Ministry of Mines and Energy
a7005.speech: Announced under-recoveries of about 82 cents per litre for petrol, 175 cents per litre for 50ppm diesel, and 166 cents per litre for 10ppm diesel, which played a vital role in the ministry's decision to increase domestic fuel prices; said the National Energy Fund will absorb remaining under-recoveries and that the ministry continues to monitor developments in international oil markets and aligns domestic prices to ensure a stable fuel supply.

a7340.speaker: Nigerien and Qatari authorities (no official statement)
a7340.name: Nigerien and Qatari authorities (no official statement)
a7340.speech: The precise details of the meeting were not made public, and no official statement followed this encounter.

a7451.speaker: GTSOU, Ukrainian gas transmission operator (published data)
a7451.name: GTSOU
a7451.title: Ukrainian gas transmission operator (published data)
a7451.speech: No delivery is scheduled for Wednesday 1 January, according to data published on Tuesday by the Ukrainian operator GTSOU, confirming the expiry of a contract established in 2019 between the company Naftogaz and the Russian giant Gazprom.

a7451.speaker: Phuc-Vinh Nguyen, head of the Energy Centre at the Jacques Delors Institute
a7451.name: Phuc-Vinh Nguyen
a7451.title: head of the Energy Centre at the Jacques Delors Institute
a7451.speech: Explains that this route represents nearly a third of the Russian gas sold to Europe.

a7451.speaker: Phuc-Vinh Nguyen, head of the Energy Centre at the Jacques Delors Institute
a7451.name: Phuc-Vinh Nguyen
a7451.title: head of the Energy Centre at the Jacques Delors Institute
a7451.speech: Confirms that by using "the geopolitical weapon of gas", Vladimir Putin "is conducting a work of sabotage; he feeds the population's resentment in order to weaken support for Ukraine and sow the seeds of discord at the European level".

a7451.speaker: Gazprom
a7451.name: Gazprom
a7451.speech: Invokes a financial dispute and refuses to consider other routes at this stage.

a7451.speaker: Cristina, 21-year-old student in Chisinau (declined to give her surname)
a7451.name: Cristina
a7451.title: 21-year-old student in Chisinau (declined to give her surname)
a7451.speech: "It's terrible, nobody knows what is going to happen. I bought candles and a generator," she told AFP.

a7451.speaker: Maia Sandu, President of Moldova
a7451.name: Maia Sandu
a7451.title: President of Moldova
a7451.speech: "The Kremlin is once again resorting to energy blackmail in order to influence the 2025 legislative elections and to weaken our European trajectory."

a7451.speaker: Maia Sandu, President of Moldova
a7451.name: Maia Sandu
a7451.title: President of Moldova
a7451.speech: Offered the inhabitants of Transdniestria, who are going to find themselves without heating in the middle of winter, "humanitarian aid".

a7451.speaker: Local authorities of Transdniestria
a7451.name: Local authorities of Transdniestria
a7451.speech: Refused the offer of humanitarian aid, hoping for a rapid resolution of the conflict.

a7451.speaker: Alexandru Flenchea, former Moldovan government official specialising in the Transdniestria region
a7451.name: Alexandru Flenchea
a7451.title: former Moldovan government official specialising in the Transdniestria region
a7451.speech: "Transdniestria is nothing other than collateral damage" in the strategy of destabilisation implemented by Russia.

a7451.speaker: Moldovan government
a7451.name: Moldovan government
a7451.speech: Announced drastic measures to reduce electricity consumption, notably by limiting the lighting of public buildings and the use of lifts, and intends to buy the missing electricity from neighbouring Romania.

a7451.speaker: European Commission
a7451.name: European Commission
a7451.speech: "The flow must be stopped on 1 January and the EU is prepared for it," the Commission told AFP on Tuesday, citing European infrastructure capable of transporting non-Russian gas "by other routes".

a7451.speaker: European Commission report published in mid-December (Brussels)
a7451.name: European Commission report published in mid-December (Brussels)

a7451.speaker: Robert Fico, Slovak Prime Minister
a7451.name: Robert Fico
a7451.title: Slovak Prime Minister
a7451.speech: "Accepting the unilateral decision of the Ukrainian president is totally irrational and wrong," he argued in a letter to Brussels, denouncing "a major financial impact" ; by way of retaliation he threatened to cut off the electricity supply that the war-torn country needs in the face of the bombardment of its energy infrastructure.

a7499.speaker: Edward Masoambeta, economic expert
a7499.name: Edward Masoambeta
a7499.title: economic expert
a7499.speech: says the intensified clampdown has pinned down illegal forex traders, creating a free flow of foreign currency as people fear engaging in black market activities: "The action by law enforcers has instilled fear among illegal traders, forcing many to abandon the market. This has resulted in the improved availability of forex."

a7499.speaker: Edward Masoambeta, economic expert
a7499.name: Edward Masoambeta
a7499.title: economic expert
a7499.speech: suggested that the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM) should consider removing certain restrictions on forex access to enhance its availability in commercial banks.

a7499.speaker: Boston Maliketi Banda, Reserve Bank of Malawi spokesperson
a7499.name: Boston Maliketi Banda
a7499.title: Reserve Bank of Malawi spokesperson
a7499.speech: disclosed that the government will soon announce measures aimed at ensuring sustained forex availability.

a7499.speaker: Market analysts
a7499.name: Market analysts
a7499.speech: attribute the trend to increased forex supply following the crackdown, with hopes that the measures will stabilize the foreign exchange market in the long term.
